review:
[h1]🎯 Огляд: Counter-Strike 2 (CS2)[/h1]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]🕹️ Геймплей[/h2]  
[i]Класика в новому тілі.[/i] CS2 зберігає дух CS:GO, але рушій Source 2 усе змінює.  
Рухи плавні, стрілянина важча, дим фізичний — все це змушує звикати навіть ветеранів.  
[i]Гра стала глибшою, але менш передбачуваною.[/i]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]🌐 Мережевий код[/h2]  
Після оновлень ситуація стала кращою — хіти реєструються стабільно.  
Але [b]64-tick[/b] усе ще тут. У 2025-му році це виглядає сумно.  
[b]Мріємо про 128-tick сервери офіційно.[/b]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]🎮 Графіка[/h2]  
Source 2 зробив гру красивою: освітлення, деталізація карт, ефекти.  
[b]Але ціна за красу — FPS.[/b]  
[i]Навіть на потужному залізі бувають дропи в самий розпал раунду.[/i]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]🚨 Античит[/h2]  
[b][u]Це головна проблема CS2.[/u][/b]  
VAC практично безсилий. Читери є навіть у Premier.  
Репорти майже не працюють, а бани — рідкість.  
[i]Без сучасного live-античита — це не кіберспортивна платформа, а рулетка.[/i]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]🐌 Оптимізація[/h2]  
[i]CS2 вимогливіша за CS:GO, але стабільності бракує.[/i]  
[b]FPS стрибає навіть на нових ПК[/b], на Overpass чи Mirage часті просідання.  
Це не той рівень, якого очікуєш від гри з мільйонами гравців.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]🛠️ Виправлення багів[/h2]  
Valve оновлює гру, але дуже повільно.  
Деякі баги існують місяцями, наприклад:

[list]
[*]зникнення зброї  
[*]непомітні хіти  
[*]ламані спавни  
[/list]

[b]Це знищує довіру навіть серед лояльних гравців.[/b]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]📌 Висновок[/h2]  
[b]Counter-Strike 2 має величезний потенціал.[/b]  
Але [i]зараз[/i] — це більше технічний бета-тест із гарною картинкою.  
Поки немає античита, стабільного FPS і регулярних патчів —  
[i]говорити про повноцінну заміну CS:GO ще рано.[/i]

[hr][/hr]

[b]⏱️ Час у грі:[/b] [i]35000+ годин[/i]

name: Apex Legends
review: I love a lot of what Apex Legends has to offer. The gun play is one of the best in any game I have ever played and the charachters are very fun. However I can’t recommend the game strictly on the monetization. For example before this new season (24) there were leaked mini battle passes for all of the new legends that would add a ton of progression that was desperately needed. It would have given the players something worth playing for. But what does EA do? Make you pay 10$ for each one. This isn’t even mentioning the collection events that cost 300+ dollars to complete. They also just added a new mobile game pay system that makes you pay to unlock something cheap and then to unlock something free. All the skins are also egregiously overpriced in general. It’s all there to just make you spend as much money as possible it’s trash. They don’t really care about the players they care about the money that’s it. The balance changes are often mediocre and  don’t always fix all the problems they should. EA is lucky the foundation of this game is as good as it is otherwise people wouldn’t put up with the gross monetization. If your a new player that know you won’t buy anything then maybe give it a try. Otherwise steer clear it’s not worth your time until EA gets it together and starts to care more about the player base.(which will never happen)

When I bought the game, previous the full release, it was interesting. Occasional discussion with people that takes it to seriously in your team, but overall it was a fun game.

Now, the game is fully packed with sweats and cheaters... and the few casuals and newbies to feed their ego. Can't recommend to a new player at all, unless you don't value your time or are a masochist. 

For casual players like me, that plays once a month at most, is a no no.

Their main problem is not the cheaters (that's normal in most online games), it's the matchmaking system which is a joke. Regardless of your skills/stats, you'll be most likely put in a match against tryharders with thousands of hours that know the exact weight of every object including their character pants, or at what angle you should shot to headshot someone hundreds of meters away with the slingshot they just found in some kid's treasure stash. 
Even though I like the challenge in games so I can improve, it's pointless since this is a battle royale, where 80% of your time is matchmaking and preparation. If matches where quick like CS would be fine.

The fix would be quite easy though. Matching people of similar stats, and then if not enough players fill it with bots. Casuals would prefer to deal with that instead of forehead web-camers.

name: Palworld
review:
A while back now I had purchased Palworld and admittedly it has been sitting inside of my Steam library for quite some time, that is until now. As a former fan of a certain other franchise that has been frequently compared to Palworld, I had basically invested in every game from that series, achieving basically 100% completion on all of them. However, around and even before 2019, I noticed a massive decline in quality, as the developers began stripping away key features and content, opting instead for gimmicks and poor world-building, writing, horrible graphics, glitched filled gameplay and more. What was once my favorite gaming franchise had basically became dead to me, as it seemed the developers cared more about profit than the quality of their games and their fan base. Also they have been making multiple attempts to disgustingly monopolize an entire gaming genre and bully and target successful competitors.

 Despite my favorite franchise now again being basically dead to me, a part of me hesitated to explore similar games because part of me still wished to see that once beloved franchise recover. Ultimately, I have given up completely of that hope. After finally playing Palworld though, I can one hundred percent say that it is an amazing game and much more unique and original than I first thought. 

 At first glance, Palworld may appear similar to that certain other franchise, but it has so much that positively let it stand on it's own. While some initial footage showcased creatures wielding guns, an aspect I wasn't particularly fond of. After about a week of playing, I've found that all of my Pals can still battle the old fashion way, with no firearms necessary but are there for those who want them. I do like that some  human characters such as in game poachers utilize guns, it's realistic and I like that.

 The graphics are pretty great I think, and I've been enjoying the multiplayer experience while hosting an online server. The world is beautifully crafted, featuring diverse locations, a variety of creatures, bosses, and an abundance of collectibles. There are also exciting events, such as for a example objects falling  from the sky for players to discover and explore. The updates have been  spectacular, greatly enhancing the game every time.

 Palworld also excels in crafting, base building, and base management, offering countless unlockables and content. However, I did notice that certain items, like some  bookcases a bathtub for example, cant be placed inside of one wall high buildings, which in my opinion could use improvement in future updates. Overall, I am greatly enjoying Palworld and believe it is a unique game that distinguishes itself in so many ways from other titles in the genre, including that one franchise, whose legal team should really stop what they are trying to do.

 I hope that the Palworld developers continue to update and add to this wonderful game and it's world. Palworld delivers and I wish only the best and great success to the development team and that they are always able to stay true to themselves and the fans and to not get lost in said success like certain other companies.

name: Palworld
review:
Alright, fellow digital demigods, I've clocked 50 glorious hours in Palworld, and my kids are still obsessed. I know efficiency, and this game is a chaotic masterpiece of it. Imagine Pokémon with guns, a dash of factory automation, and enough base-building to make your inner logistical nerd sing.

We're talking about making adorable Pals mine ore, chop trees, and even manufacture assault rifles. It's gloriously unhinged and a blast to explore with the little ones. Discovering new Pals and then equipping them with enough firepower to take down a small army is peak family bonding, trust me.

Yes, the comparisons to that other creature-collecting franchise are unavoidable, but Pocketpair has crafted something unique and incredibly fun. It's got that indie charm, a few delightful bugs, and a core loop that keeps you saying "just five more minutes" for hours on end.

To Pocketpair, I tip my virtual hardhat. You've created a genuinely addictive experience that brings a fresh, albeit ethically dubious, take to the genre. I'm wholeheartedly rooting for you in the ongoing saga against the big N. Keep those updates coming!

This game is too good for it's own sake, it sold like hotcakes on release for an almost offensively reasonable price (especially for today's standards), and has given us an insane amount of content since release. Pocketpair haven't asked for a single dime after base game purchase; and just keeps giving us more for free where most companies would nickle and dime you for simple cosmetics. Or even worse make you buy an expansion pass to access the new islands and pals *Cough* Ark *Cough*.
It's super close to that overwhelmingly positive steam review score it genuinely deserves and I beg of you to leave a positive review if you've enjoyed yourself, you can always change it if your opinion changes after all.

Palworld is a very good and fun game. As the tags says, its a open world survival creature collecting game.

Now nintendo is suing Pocketpair on the basis of PATENT infrigement. NOT COPYRIGHT; patents.
They're not coming for the Pal's design, but for gameplay elements.
In the last year, they filed patents for many of these gameplay mechanics.
And now they're coming to sue Pocketpair.

While this game has magic creatures, it mostly resembles a classic open world survival game;
you collect wood, rocks, everything to craft armor, weapons, equipment in general.
You build yourself, your base, and your team of magic creatures to fight bigger and stronger enemies.

What's there that is in common with nintedo games? The creature collecting.
But Creature collecting isn't a gameplay mechanic; it's a GENRE.
Digimon, Temtem, Coromon, Cassette Beasts, many more; these are all Creature Collecting games.
A genre cannot be patented.

If the developers of the first survival games had patented their systems, none of the great survival games we know would have been developed. Stuff like Minecraft, Terraria, Subnautica, and many more.

This game doesn't play like nintendo games. It's an action game, it's not turn based!
You also fight as your character himself, not just watch creatures fight for you!

What nintendo is doing here is evil and greedy.
They're abusing the legal system to try and take down someone that isn't even their competitor.
Palworld doesn't share a platform with their games. They're literally on separate markets.

This game is a good game, and it's very different from those others.
It's much more of a survival open world game, with Creature Collecting and base building and resource automation.
Out of all the creature collecting games that cloned nintendo's games, Palworld really isn't it.
But it's a good game, it's fun, it was ever since its first release. It's still in active development, and gets updated regularly. Its developers focus on the player's fun, and have greatly succeded.
I trust them to keep doing a good job, if they're not stopped by this legal abuse coming from greedy old talentless people that have kept making the same stale game for decades.

review:
I've got many issues to address
1. Losing Main Mission progress of a player / friend that joins your lobby: I am writing this first because this is the issue that made me write this review, there is a high probability chance if you are playing with a friend that the next time they join the same exact server, exactly where you left off, their main mission just disappears and is replaced by a Japanese stand in of a mission example. There is not a single way known to the community to resolve this except "starting from scratch". If this was a new issue I wouldn't be writing this but this issue has been addressed to be fixed mid 2024. So if you are planing to play this game with anybody, do not buy the game, also having a dedicated server will probably avoid this problem.

2. The game is an extreme grind fest, every now and then you'll be locked of progressing your base because you are lacking levels

3. The main selling point of this game is the exploration and capturing new Pal's and possibly combat using guns ETC, instead, you will be stuck in your base 80% of the time either waiting for something to be crafted / completed, checking if your egg has hatched, checking if a raid has completed because some items you cannot easily grind and worst of it all, checking if your Pal's are depressed / working / hungry all the time and providing the necessary food resources for them.

4. F simulator, you are required to hold F for everything, and sometimes its literally for an hour depending if you got a recepie and you finally grinded the hell out of the game for the materials you are lacking, sometimes you will just want to instantly go explore but you are missing bullets for your weapon, good luck waiting for the 200 bullets to be made so you can actually use the gun at all, and if you want to speed up the process (helping your pals) you'll literally be stuck holding the button F, and I do mean HOLDING, because if you arent holding you arenot doing anything.

5. Stamina limits the main selling points of the game to an insane extent that you cannot even play properly

6. Stats, all the stats you can upgrade on your player are absolutely useless except Carry Weight and Staminda, and after that putting the rest into HP because upgraidng other stats such as ATK or Work Speed doesn't do anything

The game is constantly forcing you to spend more time to achieve anything, and its not even spending time the way you want it to, catching new pals, getting stronger, discovering new pals, you are forced to spend your time in the most boring way possible

Ofcourse most of these issues could potentially be fixed by Mods or Cheats, but if a game requires you to make macros to actually enjoy the game, is it even worth it ?

If you are planing to defend the game because its "Early Access", so is another of their games "Craftopia" since 2020, and oh boy have they "done" something about that game, its no excuse to leave a game breaking bug that literally requires you to start from scratch out for a year

Oh and the guns you are so excited to use ? You wont be using them until you grind for hours into the game

I do not think this game is worth the money and worst of all I do not think this game is fun enough for its price.

Sure sometimes when you actually get the chance to explore once you've stored enough food in your base not to care, and when you discover brand new Pal's that are slightly stronger than yours, and you actually get to explore the world and the Pal's, it can be fun. But these moments in the game last so short because your inventory will get filled and you gotta go back to your base, running into a new daily life activity that can be simplified to "Did I make dinner, did I put things in the freezer, did I turn off the Oven, did I set my alarm for tomorrow, did I do chores" over and over again

But in the very end, even the bosses are just fat punching bags that just last long so you would spend more hours into the game unnecessarily

Suppose I should do a review...
Okay, so this is one of those games where you don't need any level of experience beyond just standard PvP FPS stuff to get into it. However,
-paid content includes having fun, in-game chat*, storing more than a handful of items
-lots and lotsa toxic players, they don't normally interact with people beyond dominating lobbies though
-source(TM)  jank©
Jank includes anything from the unintended demoknight, battle medic and Pootis sub-classes all the way to backstab flings, that one window on pl_frontier, and a lot of weird reasons for getting stuck on things. The game traces its roots back to a HL2 mod and as such has matured over a long time. There's a grand old well of user generated content you can get into for free on a lot of community servers, which is a great way to have fun or play warioware if you don't want to pay for it. Seriously, check out the custom maps people make, it's incredible. 

Game culture you might want to know about: 
-Friendlies: usually seen dancing in groups, crouching with melee weapons or doing other funny shit. Killing them is normally rude, unless the whole server is dancing. At that point, I'd consider it okay to re-queue for something else or start using your tauntkills.
-Pootis: a quasi-friendly species, the Pootis is found in ctf_2Fort and many other gardens of slow gameplay. Though some are un-adorned heavy players, one can easily tell a pootis by their behaviour and colourful, often whimsical plumage. They most typically sport a beanie with tassels and a sandvich in hand, with other colourful garments seen often. They are typically friendlies. If you attack them, they may stop at nothing to kill you in a demeaning way. They may attack first, in which case the winner is whoever tauntkills the other first.
-If someone dies suddenly, with no attacks made, they have used a 'killbind'. It is a common joke. To make your own:
     1- open settings from within the game. From the popup for changing controls, select [Advanced...] -> [enable developer console]
     2- with the console enabled, hit `~ key (top left of keyboard)
     3- don't worry about the code, you're not going to hack anything (probably)
     4- enter this phrase without the quotes: 'bind k kill' and press enter
                         (you can select another key to bind but k is easy to remember and not used by default)
     5- disable the developer console, it's really annoying mid-game.

name: Team Fortress 2
review:
Team Fortress 2 - what firstly started as a nostalgic dive into a game of my childhood quickly turned into an appreciation post about how a game soon turning 20 years old can still be relevant and most balanced hero shooter out there.

Seriously, the game's balance is amazing, except sniper, its always sniper. That aside you can put any 2 classes against each other and both of them have a chance to win. Don't get me wrong there are types of soft and hard counters amongst the classes but depending on the positioning you take and how you decide to play with your strengths and weaknesses you have a chance to win even against hard counters of your class or at least to regroup with your team. On top of that there is variety of subclasses and interesting sidegrades of different weapons.

The problems the game had in the past e.g. Meet the Match update that removed quickplay, the whole botting thing that made casual unplayable etc. are long gone and I can proudly say casual is great. Player numbers might not be as high as they used to be, but if you fiddle with the map settings you will never notice any difference. The maps that used to be popular back when i started (2013) are still popular nowadays.

Oh did I mention that in tf2 you can mod almost anything ? Ranging from custom huds and crosshairs to custom models and hit sounds tf2 mods are on another level. I would definetly recommend using one of the huds made by the community - most famous probably being [b] budhud [/b].

Only downside that seems glaring to me is that if you are brand new player you might have harder time playing as the player base skill level has risen over the years, to which I can assure you that this game suprisingly so, has hidden MMR for casual and you will not meet them in every match. 

9/10 just because the devs don't treat it as they should - as a gem.

[h1][b][u]Same Gun, Different Skin: The Stale Theater of Call of Duty[/u][/b][/h1]


After dragging myself through yet another Call of Duty, it’s safe to say the franchise has fully embraced being a live-service treadmill. You launch the game, get bombarded with six menus, a battle pass you didn’t ask for, and a launcher that feels like a mobile store in disguise.

The last campaign I played was Modern Warfare III, that's the moment I mentally checked out. Not because I finished it, but because it stopped even pretending to be a campaign. The so-called "Open Combat Missions" were just recycled multiplayer maps awkwardly stitched together with half-hearted voice lines and objectives that felt like someone wrote them five minutes before a deadline. I literally spawned in and thought, “Wait, this is just a Domination map, isn’t it?” And it was. Same map, different wrapper. You could go loud or stealth, but it didn’t matter. The enemies barely noticed either way, and the mission structure had all the tension of a tutorial.

Modern Warfare 2019 at least made an effort to give Farah and Price a bit of narrative weight. The follow-up, MWII, started to drift and lose focus, offering more spectacle but less direction. By the time I reached MWIII, the story had flatlined. It felt like leftover DLC reheated in the marketing department and sold as a campaign. Any sense of ambition had already left the building.

Multiplayer still feels mechanically solid, but actual fun is another story. Win one match and you’re suddenly dropped into a lobby full of slide-canceling stream monsters who treat every round like a tournament final. Lose, and you get dumped into a pity match with bots. Skill-Based Matchmaking doesn't ease you into anything. It yanks you around like a malfunctioning carnival ride. There’s no sense of progression, just constant overcorrection.

Trying to navigate it all through Call of Duty HQ is its own kind of boss fight. Want to play the campaign? Wrong menu. Looking for Zombies? Wrong tab again. The launcher feels like it was designed by a marketing team that’s never played a game. Everything important is buried under store banners and battle pass promotions that blink like neon signs at a mobile casino.

And Zombies? Once a standout, creative mode full of tension and chaos, it used to play like a haunted side quest in Warzone. You’d grind contracts, loot armor, and repeat the same tired loop. It wasn’t scary. It wasn’t clever. It was just another mode built around seasonal rewards. Sure, Black Ops 6 brought back the round-based format, and that’s nice for nostalgia. But the experience still feels hollow. It’s less like survival and more like checking off a chore list while being chased by rubber skeletons.

Black Ops 6 launched in October 2024. Now we’re barely eight months in and Black Ops 7 is already looming. I get that Call of Duty is annual, but this feels frantic. No breathing room, no time to reflect or evolve, just slap on a new number and reset the store.

And let’s talk about that store. That’s where the real energy goes. Anime skins, glowing rifles, limited-time EDM bundles, all shoved front and center. Meanwhile, maps, modes, and features are recycled, relabeled, and resold. Want an old favorite map? It’s back, now “remastered,” and probably locked behind a premium pack.

Call of Duty isn’t about gameplay anymore. It’s about retention. It’s a marketplace wrapped in a first-person shooter skin. They say "next gen storytelling," but the only story being told here is one of diminishing returns and growing shop menus.

What hurts most is that the gunplay still feels good. Movement is crisp. Weapons snap with satisfying weight. The polish is there, buried under all the systems that suck the fun out. You can tell there’s still a great shooter hidden inside this mess. It just isn’t allowed to breathe anymore.

I picked up the Modern Warfare packs out of stubborn hope. But when I saw how they were pitching Black Ops 6, it all clicked. Another flashy trailer. Another beta access pre-order. Another wave of grind passes and FOMO bundles. No thanks. I’m not falling for that again.

They could bring back round-based Zombies. They could refine the movement. They could even polish the UI. But until they go back to the roots, with proper campaigns, balanced matchmaking, and content over cosmetics, I’m done giving them full price. Unless it’s 90 percent off and comes with a handwritten apology, I’m out.

📜 SIDE NOTES:

[code][b]⭐Multiplayer feels sharp and responsive, but Skill-Based Matchmaking ensures every match turns into a sweaty, hypercompetitive esports trial that punishes casual players and kills the fun.
⭐ Zombies may be round-based again, but it still feels less like surviving the undead and more like ticking off a grocery list while being awkwardly chased by decorative Halloween props.
⭐ The campaign plays painfully safe and has all the emotional impact of a wet paper towel, stumbling through objectives like it's speedrunning a checklist for an interview it forgot to prepare for.
⭐ The movement is buttery smooth, which is great if you enjoy gliding gracefully through a maze of recycled content, pointless objectives, relentless grind, and overpriced anime skins for days.[/b] [/code]
[code][b]⚠️ Black Ops 6 adds some quality-of-life improvements and delivers a more familiar Zombies experience, but it doesn't go far enough to justify its place in the annual cycle. The pacing, monetization, and matchmaking fatigue all remain front and center.[/b] [/code]
[code][b]📢 There are still no significant changes to address the core problems that drove players away in the first place. Unless I were a die-hard fan, which I’m not anymore, or found it in a heavy discount bin, Black Ops 6 doesn’t earn my full price or full attention. I highly doubt Black Ops 7 will either![/b] [/code]

name: New World: Aeternum
review:
I really wanted to love this game.
I remember the hype, the trailers, the idea of a new MMO that could finally break the mold — something fresh, something exciting.

And for a few hours... it was exciting.
The world is beautiful, the combat feels responsive, and the soundtrack hits just right. But after that?
It’s like a beautiful shell with nothing inside.

The grind is unbearable.
Not the fun kind of grind where you feel rewarded after hours — I’m talking about repetitive, copy-paste quests like "kill 10 of these" and "gather 5 of those"... over and over.
And the worst part? Most of them send you running across the map for 15 minutes just to collect something that takes 30 seconds.

The economy? Broken.
Crafting felt meaningful at first — until you realize that everyone’s crafting the same gear and undercutting each other.
Gold inflation, useless items, and towns that can’t even be maintained because players stop caring after a while.

PvP?
Fun for a bit, until you realize how much of it is dominated by zergs, exploits, and imbalance.
If you're solo or casual, forget about being competitive.

But what really broke it for me wasn’t the bugs, the lag, or even the bots.
It was this lingering feeling of emptiness.
Like you're grinding and grinding... for what?
The story is forgettable, the world doesn’t evolve, and after a while, you just feel like you’re playing out of habit, not enjoyment.

I kept telling myself,

“It’ll get better with the next patch.”
“The devs are listening.”
“Maybe next content drop will fix it.”

But weeks turned into months, and I just stopped logging in.

Is it the worst MMO out there?
No.
But it’s a reminder that pretty graphics and good mechanics mean nothing if the soul isn’t there.
I didn’t quit because it was hard.
I quit because it was empty.

name: New World: Aeternum
review:
Beautiful but Broken: A Stunning MMO Undone by Its Own Systems

At first glance, this game is breathtaking. The visual quality is top-tier – environments are richly detailed, and I have to give special praise to the dungeon design. The atmosphere, lighting, and visual storytelling in those areas truly blew me away while exploring the game for the first time. It felt like there was something magical here – something worth investing time in.

And yet, as I reached the later stages of the game, that initial wonder began to fade. What replaced it was something much less enchanting: a system built around grind, RNG, and what feels like a casino-inspired loot loop.

Inventory Hell
Let’s start with the biggest flaw: the inventory system. It's a mess. You spend an absurd amount of time just sorting through endless piles of junk – useless armor, weapons, and trinkets that serve no purpose. There's no satisfying way to sell or discard them. It’s not just clutter; it actively kills momentum and enjoyment. In WoW, even bad loot had a reason to exist. Here, it’s just digital garbage.

Combat and Progression
The combat is actually good – smooth, responsive, and enjoyable. But the progression is bizarrely lopsided. Leveling is way too fast and easy, while gathering professions like mining become a painful, drawn-out grind. It feels like two separate games – one rushing you forward, the other dragging you back.

Disconnected World, Shallow Exploration
Despite the beautiful locations, the world feels oddly disconnected. There's no meaningful interaction with the environment, no real sense of presence. You don’t need to explore, and once you've seen an area, there’s little reason to return. The world is too small, too static. New zones should be arriving yearly, along with a steady flow of new dungeons and raids – not just recycled ones with increased difficulty.

From Immersion to Slot Machines
This is where the real disappointment hits. The game slowly shifts from immersive MMO to something that feels designed around loot crate addiction. The gameplay ends up revolving around opening boxes, hoping for a lucky drop – like a slot machine in a 24/7 convenience store. That kind of design breaks the fantasy, breaks the immersion, and ultimately breaks the game.

Economy in Chaos
The auction house is another weak link. Because of the nonsensical item system, prices are wildly inconsistent. It’s difficult to judge value, and trading becomes more frustrating than rewarding. It’s a symptom of the game’s deeper design issues.

Bright Spots Still Exist
To be fair, there are elements worth celebrating. The voice-acted NPC dialogue during story quests is a huge plus. Hearing characters speak adds a layer of immersion and personality that plain text just can’t deliver – and it genuinely made me care more about the main story, at least at first. More MMOs should do this.

World bosses and live events also shine – for brief moments, you feel part of a living, breathing community. And the musical instruments and group performances? Pure genius. These systems are fun, original, and show a glimpse of the game’s untapped potential.

Conclusion: A Lost Opportunity
This game could have been one of the greats. It had the budget, the engine, the setting. For a while, it looked like it might truly rival the giants of the genre. But over time, poor design choices, inventory frustration, and a shift toward “casino-style” systems have dragged it down.

It’s beautiful, but broken. A haunting reminder of how potential means nothing without vision.

name: Black Myth: Wukong
review:
Overall, incredibly fun game. It's beautiful, the storytelling is fantastic (if you like the Journey to the west), the combat is (mostly) fluid, and upgrades feel like they mean something.

My cons are that once you hit chapter 4, boss fights start getting REALLY cheesy. You don't have much in your arsenal to deal with flying enemies and the game exploits this weakness ad nauseam. Bosses will float in the air for minutes at a time throwing attacks at you so you just sit there and wait/dodge until they're done, or use on or your forms only to have them do it again a few minutes later.

There's also an incredibly annoying amount of stun locking/staggering where you'll still be in the animation of being hit only for the game to track you with a ranged attack that hits you the frame before you can dodge again.

I wish this game gave you more tools to deal with enemies in the air and character verticality in general. For a monkey, you can't jump for **** and climbing isn't even an option.

Having said all that, it's a great game that lives comfortably in between Souls and Sekiro for mobility, fast action, and how punishing mistakes are.

Get it when it's on sale again just because I think it's snaky that they've waited more than a year to put the game on sale. If they wait this long again, there will be twice as many alternative options to play that are just as good or better than this.

name: Black Myth: Wukong
review:
I wanted to like it, but I just can't. The game crashes every 20-30 minutes with no error message, even though I have a high-end PC. I could understand this if it had just been released, but it's been a year. I had to launch it three times before it finally ran, only to then get an error message during the shader loading phase. The framerate is low, and while you can lower the graphics, it's a shame for a game whose main strength is its visuals. I spent about 20 minutes just trying to get the settings right. Suffice to say, I wasn't in the best mood and was already exhausted before even playing.

The game finally became playable:

The visuals are gorgeous, the enemies design are amazing, but the level design SUCKS. I only got to the first biome (the forest), but the level is filled with arbitrary invisible walls for seemingly no reason, punishing players who try to explore. Coupled with the fact that the enemies, apart from bosses, are super easy, this makes the map useless. It essentially becomes an exclusive boss rush. I like Dark Souls, so I appreciate boss fights, but only boss fights? Not for me. I didn't even like the gameplay; it felt like I was just mashing buttons and hoping to dodge. The attacks are so unpredictable because, unlike Dark Souls, the bosses have many more quicker attacks and some unexpected ones. It felt incredibly punishing and frustrating. Even after beating a boss, I didn't feel good because I knew it was more about luck, and I'd also gained XP from killing the super-easy mobs on the way to them.

The map is only gorgeous thanks to Unreal Engine 6; otherwise, it's just a generic forest, and the random invisible walls make exploration pointless.

Also, I feel like  nobody is talking about the atrocious blurry area around the main character when rotating the camera, ruin so much the experience of appreciating the top notch graphic... (I tried to set different setting but it was still there and most gameplay I seen online has the same issue)

I feel like the game benefited from a lot of hype and filled a void left by big companies releasing consecutive poor games. The manufactured "woke scandal" also helped make the game look even better.

Ultimately, I hope the company does well and I'm glad about their success, but I didn't like the game (and the crashes are still not fixed). I don't recommend it.

TL;DR: An Unreal Engine 6 tech demo focused on boss fights, wrapped in amazing mythology. Amazing graphics and effect is not enough for me to enjoy a game.

(Oh, and by the way, [spoiler] you only play as Wukong for the first 10 minutes. You then play as a generic, silent monkey. If you were expecting the eccentric, funny Wukong personality throughout your journey, you're going to be disappointed. [/spoiler])

review:
When I bought this game on the Steam Summer Sale a few years ago, I was at a bit of a low point in my life and through it, I was able to connect with a bunch of people who also enjoyed the game. Even though I don't talk with many of them anymore, the memories I made on this game are irreplaceable.

Besides my personal experience with the game, this game has proven time and time again to be not only one of the best zombie games out there, but also one of the best co-op games as well. Unlike a lot of zombie games that seem to play the same way, Left 4 Dead provides a unique experience that focuses on teamwork and is still fun to play even today, despite the game having released all the way back in 2008. I was never a fan of tactical games like Counter Strike or R6S due to the mechanical skills needed to keep up with your team and Left 4 Dead provided a fun experience that leaned further on team coordination rather than how fast a survivor could shoot an enemy or how fast their reaction time is while turning a corner. Along with this, Left 4 Dead has a colorful cast of characters who are all vibrant and stand out from each other. The story is also unique compared to other zombie apocalypse stories and allows you to take in the details as quickly or slowly as you'd like with Valve's mastery in environmental storytelling and dialog.

The other aspect I love about this game is the workshop and how much mod support the game has. Of course things can get janky with how stretched the engine is on this game, but the amount of custom campaigns, survivor swaps, weapon skins, custom mutations, and so much more never ceases to amaze me. My favorite custom campaign has to be the Crash Bandicoot campaign and is also the very first custom campaign I played. I can't even count how many times I've played this campaign and it's become an unforgettable part of my experience in Left 4 Dead 2.

While I've had a falling out with a few of the friends I've played this with over the years, I still find myself coming back to this game either to experience the fun I had back then again, or make new memories. This game, along with Valve's other titles stand as a testament to how far a game with a good set of developers and a loyal community can go. As of writing this, I hope to get more out of this game with each time I press play. I've played games for almost my whole life, and I've come to learn that games are art and should be experienced that way. Left 4 Dead 2 only reinforces that idea in me and I hope to make new memories on this game, wherever life takes me next.

Go from point A to point B without dying.
That's it.
That’s the game.
But in practice?

It’s a test of willpower, a hellish gauntlet, and a psychological experiment to see how fast a human being can scream “WHY DID YOU SHOOT THE CAR ALARM?!”

THE SURVIVORS
You get four playable characters, none of whom asked for this:

Coach – your friendly local diabetic gym teacher with a heart of gold and cholesterol of steel.

Nick – a con artist in a white suit. He is sleaze incarnate.

Rochelle – the most underappreciated and overmodded survivor on Nexus.

Ellis – a southern himbo whose brain has been replaced with NASCAR trivia and stories about Keith.

By the way, you can mod any of them to be Master Chief, Hatsune Miku, or 12-foot anime dommies — and you will.

THE ZOMBIES
The zombies come in two flavors:

Regular zombies, also known as "expendable XP drops."

Special Infected, also known as:

Boomer – a fat man who throws up on you and then explodes.

Hunter – edgy parkour boy who hates you specifically.

Smoker – stealthy smoker who ropes you like it’s a hentai.

Jockey – tiny gremlin that mounts your skull and rides you into the nearest death pit.

Spitter – spits radioactive gender fluid.

Charger – legally classified as a war crime.

Tank – a muscle-bound gorilla that throws concrete and has the HP of a small country.

Witch – a crying one-shot boss fight that you will startle every time despite being warned.

The AI Director controls everything dynamically.
Have too much ammo? Spawns a Tank.
Got too many medkits? Here’s a Witch.
Doing too well? Here’s all of them at once in a hallway the size of a prison toilet.

GAME MODES
Campaign – Classic co-op. Get in, survive, get out.

Versus – Human players control zombies. Betray your friends. Laugh as you body them with a single Charger.

Survival – How long can you survive endless waves? Answer: 13 seconds.

Scavenge – Team deathmatch, but with gas cans. Pure chaos.

Realism – No HUD. No outlines. No mercy. Like being born in the woods and told to read Nietzsche.

And then there’s Mutation Modes, including:

Chainsaw Massacre (self-explanatory),

Gib Fest (M60s for everyone),

Confogl (competitive tryhard simulator),

And my personal favorite: Hard Eight, where the game spawns twice the infected and none of the hope.

MODDING COMMUNITY
The real game isn’t in the gameplay — it’s in the workshop.
You haven’t truly played Left 4 Dead 2 until you’ve replaced:

The Tank with Shrek,

The music with "All Star,"

The Jockey with a toddler riding a Roomba,

The pistol sounds with anime moaning,

And the survivors with every combination of Doomguy, Thomas the Tank Engine, and a 2B swimsuit mod.

You can install 100GB of mods, crash your RAM, and still run it better than CS2.

SOUND DESIGN
The sounds are iconic:

The Witch’s sobbing is actual psychological warfare.

The Tank’s music triggers the fight-or-flight response in war veterans.

And every time you hear “Grabbing pills!” your brain releases serotonin.

Also:

Molotovs explode like Zeus himself took offense to your existence.
Pipe bombs make a beeping sound that attracts zombies and gives me war flashbacks.
The Charger sounds like he’s running through drywall and masculinity.

WHY IS IT STILL ALIVE?
Left 4 Dead 2 is 14 years old.
It runs on a toaster.
It still has an active player base.
People host tournaments.
People mod it daily.
And Valve keeps patching it, which is more effort than they’ve put into Half-Life 3.

There is no progression.
No battle pass.
No cosmetics.
Just skill. Violence. And a deep-seated hatred for Boomers.

FINAL THOUGHTS
Left 4 Dead 2 is:

The most fun you’ll ever have yelling at your friends.

A perfect co-op game that still has zero competition.

A love letter to the genre that somehow still has the best zombie AI in gaming.

A showcase of how modding = immortality.

This isn’t just a game.
This is a stress test for your friendships and a religious experience for anyone who’s ever thrown a bile bomb into a funnel of undead.
I give Left 4 Dead 2:

10 out of 10 adrenaline shots.
One panicked scream when someone startles the Witch.
And a slow clap for Coach, who still hasn’t stopped running.

As always, more content to come.
So stay tuned.

Witam, prawda!

Tu Krwawy Joe i dziś opowiem wam o grze, która nie tylko przetrwała próbę czasu, ale wręcz rozkwita wśród zgliszczy współczesnych shooterów – Left 4 Dead 2. Tak, moi mili, ta perełka od Valve wciąż żyje, kopie i rozwala nieumarłych z gracją, której nie powstydziłby się sam Bruce Campbell.

Zacznijmy od tego, że L4D2 to esencja kooperacyjnego grania. Czterech ocalałych, hordy zarażonych, napięcie jak przy rozbrajaniu bomby i ta nieustanna potrzeba trzymania się razem – tu nie ma miejsca dla samotnych wilków. Gra nagradza współpracę i karze egoizm, a każda sesja to inna historia, dzięki niesamowitemu systemowi AI Director, który dostosowuje tempo i poziom trudności w czasie rzeczywistym.

Broń? Miodzio. Od klasycznych shotgunów po katanę, patelnię i piłę mechaniczną – każda zabawka ma swój ciężar i feeling. A jak walniesz z molotova w środek hordy i zobaczysz te jęzory ognia... Poezja!

Tryby? Jest kampania, tryb przetrwania, versus, mutacje – każdy znajdzie coś dla siebie. A modderska scena to złoto – nowe mapy, skiny, tryby... Można grać bez końca.

A klimat? Ten brudny, amerykański południowy posmak apokalipsy zombie. Muzyka, dialogi, głosy postaci – wszystko pasuje idealnie, jak celny headshot z magnuma.

Podsumowując: Left 4 Dead 2 to nie tylko klasyk. To gra, która dalej kopie tyłki i pokazuje, jak robić kooperacyjne shootery z duszą. Jeśli jeszcze nie grałeś – nadrób to natychmiast. Jeśli grałeś – wróć. Bo zombie same się nie odstrzelą, prawda?

Z pozdrowieniami – Krwawy Joe.

review:
Let's start with the visuals. Prepare to be amazed by the stunningly blocky graphics that would make Picasso question his artistic choices. It's like someone turned a potato into a pixelated masterpiece and ran with it. Who knew that a world full of squares and rectangles could be so captivating?

Now, don't let the charming art style fool you. The game packs a punch when it comes to challenges. From fending off brain-hungry zombies to scavenging for toilet paper (yes, even in the apocalypse, that's a thing), Unturned throws curveballs at you faster than a clumsy outfielder.

But fear not, for the game's survival mechanics are as easy to grasp as a greased pig. You'll quickly learn the art of crafting weapons out of unlikely objects, building fortresses that would make Tony Stark proud, and driving vehicles that handle like drunk shopping carts. It's a recipe for chaos, and it tastes oh-so-delicious.

The multiplayer aspect is where Unturned truly shines. Grab your friends and jump into the madness together. Team up to create the most absurd bases, engage in epic battles that resemble a circus on steroids, or embark on zany quests that make you question your life choices. It's the kind of multiplayer experience that leaves you crying tears of laughter and wondering why you didn't become a professional clown.

Unturned on Steam is a game that never takes itself seriously, and that's precisely why it's so damn fun. It's a wild rollercoaster ride through a blocky wonderland, where laughter is your best weapon and silliness is your survival strategy.

So, if you're looking for a game that will tickle your funny bone and make your friends question your sanity, look no further. Unturned is here to make you laugh, cry (from laughing too hard), and question why you ever took gaming so seriously in the first place. Embrace the absurdity and embark on this hilarious journey. Your inner comedian will thank you.

Lost Ark – 1,000+ Hours Later
Incredible game held back by bad systems.

Lost Ark has the best ARPG combat and animations I’ve ever seen. The classes are fun, PvE is challenging, and the raids and dungeons are well-designed. The art and character design are top-notch, and the small group content makes connecting with others easier.

But there are two big issues:

Pay-to-win is real. Over time, the game shifted to heavily reward spending money, especially if you want to keep up with guilds or higher-end content.

The grind is brutal. Managing multiple characters daily feels more like a chore than fun, and the constant FOMO wears you down.

review:
TL;DR: A great game, but way too expensive

First off, the biggest positive of this game (for me) - it has the most satisfying combat system in an ARPG I have played. The skills are visually intensive, feel impactful, powerful. The boss fights are good, often have individual mechanics while being readable and well telegraphed. Learning a new raid is a satisfying experience, playing a raid is a satisfying experience. Getting into one - not so much.

And this is where it all goes downhill. The game has multiple gear progression systems, which are both mandatory (to the point you can't enter an encounter without meeting some requirements) and VERY expensive. This creates a pretty unpleasant environment for players who don't want to spend either too much money or too much time in the game. And to make things worse, spending only too much time doesn't cut it. You get enough to meet the "minimum requirements" for the most recent content, but nowhere near enough to be considered "strong". As a result, the LFG experience is often extremely frustrating. You can legitimately spend more time trying to join or gather a group than you spend afterwards playing the raid. 

This is what drove me away from the game in the end. I was playing the maximum allowed 6 characters in the endgame in order to maximize my income so that I could stay at the "poorly geared" category. It's exhausting and not worth it, despite the satisfying experience of the actual gameplay.

I would gladly go back to the game in case they make a major overhaul of the endgame structure, scrap the multiple-character gold earning and reduce the power gap between the free-to-play users and the whales. Which is probably not happening, so I'll probably keep playing other games instead.

Hello, non-Steam War Thunder player here with 3,500 hours on file.
Pros: tanks look cool
Cons: Numerous and varied.
- The current server architecture is absolutely unstable at an inherently painful level. Movement issues, input lag, random server spikes across the board (that the entire server talks about in chat for 5 laggy, painful minutes), the ancient GHOST SHELL BUG, feature of multiple 'ITS FIXED!' reports (no it fucking isn't) and now a litany of stupid microjitters AND/OR invisible solid objects on maps which are just oh, so fun to drive into. Oh, and the lack of an Australian server (South Asia Ping? 180 if you're lucky. Packet loss? 10% minimum at peak times), but that's a personal peeve.

- Gaijin cannot possibly fathom the concept of gameplay innovation. If they'd instead consider the homeless man outside their offices, bashing away with a dustbin lid, this might change, because there are very, very few gamemodes actually populated beyond the basic 4; because those gamemodes outside the basic 4, fucking suck, because they're 'unpopulated' and 'nobody plays those, so why would we innovate on them and introduce fun new mechanics? Nah, add dozer blades to like a dozen tanks instead.' Those basic 4 are also extremely boring. Air Realistic is completely unplayable for bombers above 9.0, nullifying massive swathes of playable aircraft and relegating them to the bin, Ground Realistic is an exercise in not being hit by an exorbitantly bullshit projectile that violated several laws of the games' physics engine in order to save server performance and Arcade is effectively the only playable, enjoyable game mode - that doesn't give you enough progression to warrant playing it, because the length of time to grind above 5.0 is, funnily enough, reminiscent of a snail's pace.

- Predatory marketing taken to notable extremes. Do you want to progress in this game? Your time-to-grind will be more than halved with a Premium account. Premium account promotions are shovelled absolutely anywhere they can be. And it's fucking expensive, even OFF the Steam branch of this game (which incurs additional fees) the purchasable currency, advancements, premium account, etc etc, are all batshit insane expensive. Oh, AND, $120 AUD for a fucking F/A-18? Seriously? Or a Leopard 2A-whogivesafuck? Or a boat? $120? I shamefully admit I've thrown a disgusting amount of money at this game but I must admit, I regret those purchases and the support for this company resultant. No more.

I strongly advise against picking this up. Go elsewhere, like MTC4 on Roblox, or GHPC once it shows promise.

review:
Disclaimer for the reviews speaking on performance: Since the release of title update 2, the performance has massively increased and the game has returned to a playable state. 

This game is (nearly) perfect. the monsters are all fantastic, the combat is fun and engaging, the larger and more open levels have made for more fun on the side of exploration, and the weather system is a very nice touch.

The major criticism that I along with many others have is that the game is hilariously easy. I thought monster hunter rise was lacking in real challenge, but this one takes the cake. I'm not sure if its the large number of QOL features or simply that the combat system works too well, or perhaps its that none of the monsters aside from the late game ones have any real meat to them. for me, Low rank felt like "fischer price: my first monster hunter" and high rank introduced some moderate challenge, but moderate is all id say it is. it isn't until after you beat the main story that the game gives you *some* difficulty. i'm sure for less experienced players the perception will be much different , but thats how it was for me. to be fair, there's always further updates as well as a DLC to anticipate. i'm sure capcom will find a way to add in some extra flavor by then. 

That said, its a perfect introduction to the series. for any new players interested in playing their first monster hunter game, this one shouldn't disappoint.

review:
Unlike many other people, I'm pretty satisfied with the gameplay, and don't mind the easier difficulty compared to the older titles. While the graphics are downright terrible for a 2025 release, I've never cared about graphics that much, so that wasn't a huge concern for me. 

What I do take issue with however is that we have borderline PS3 level graphics that require ridiculous hardware to run even remotely acceptable. Third party fixes greatly helped the massive stuttering issues, but with the recent game updates they seem less and less effective. And even at 4k with DLAA it doesn't look impressive at all.

Currently the main issue seems to be their DLSS implementation. It was horrible from day 1 with bad artifacting, subpar image quality and performance. Though by manually swapping DLL versions you could remedy these issues. Right now that's not working though. FSR works a LOT better, but sadly it's not the latest version either.

After people did it through third party mods, they finally implemented an option for you to use DLSS upscaling with FSR frame generation. Propably because they knew they messed it up somehow. This is definitely the best setting for my end as well.

I did 100% the game because I had plenty of fun but with the performance getting worse and worse recently, I can't bring myself to even check the new updates anymore.

TLDR; I do like this game a lot, but the devs need to step up their game. This is not a product that can be sold to consumers in good conscience and it really is all up to the performance.

name: Monster Hunter Wilds
review:
I've seen many people complaining about the game, so I'm here to put the rumors to rest and bring the truth to light. A lot of the complaints are about computers not being able to run the game or frequent crashes—but that's not the game's fault. In my personal experience, the very few times the game crashed were during startup, which isn’t uncommon when I run a game for the first time. So I wasn’t too surprised. It typically happens before I even begin playing. The game has crashed on me about three times while starting up, but as I said earlier, this usually happens the first time I run a game. One issue that may occur after startup is the slow loading of the map, characters, armor, etc., but this is due to the high number of polygons—which isn’t necessarily a bad thing. If you don’t have to wait for things to load, congrats! Your system is handling it well.

Now, let’s talk about what happens after starting the game. The player's character has a wide range of customization options. You can tweak nearly every feature of your character’s face with a high level of freedom. Beyond character customization, you also have access to a variety of amazing armor and weapon options. There are many different weapons to suit many playstyles. If you ever want to switch weapons, you can—you’re free to own as many different weapons as you like, though you can only equip two at a time. I do find the weapon attacks and combos to be [b]super[/b] repetitive. I've had a few friends watch me play the game, and they always ask, "Why do you keep doing the same attack?" Well, it's because there really aren’t many other moves to use. It's kind of a "one-trick pony" situation, if that makes sense. At first, it didn’t really strike me—until my friends pointed it out. Then I started thinking about it and realized they were right. It’s just like, “Slash attack a million times to defeat the monster. Oh, and once every century, I get to jump on its back and do this awesome, peak animation.” It makes me feel like a fucking potato rolling around in circles with no point in life sometimes.

There are many different types of armor, each offering different benefits. You obtain armor by hunting a variety of interesting and unique monsters. One feature I really appreciate is that armor is not gender-locked. Some games have female armor that just doesn’t look great, but here, you can wear what you like regardless of your character’s gender. While some armor designs may appear more masculine or feminine, there are also more androgynous options available. 

When hunting monsters for armor, they don’t just drop a helmet or chest plate—you need to collect materials from them. Sometimes, this means hunting the same monster multiple times to gather everything you need. Each monster has unique attack patterns and special skills. They also have specific weak points you can target to gain additional materials or break off body parts, which can weaken them or disable certain attacks. Monsters aren’t just used to craft armor; you can also use their materials to forge weapons. However, not all weapons can be crafted from all monsters. As far as I know, every monster can be used to create armor. 

The NPCs in the game each have distinct designs, and the story is full of adventure and companionship. I feel that at some (many) moments the story ticks me off. [b]Huge spoiler upcoming[/b] : [spoiler] Like what do you mean you're suddenly forgiving that monster and mad at me for defeating it? [/spoiler]

The next part of my review contains [b] SPOILERS. [/b]
[spoiler] You get to keep two pet-like companions throughout your journey: the Palico you start with, and your Seikret. Another companion who joins you is Alma, an NPC who doesn’t fight alongside you but follows you on her own Seikret, which she unlocks at the same time as you unlock yours. You can customize all the colors of both your Palico and Seikret. The Palico has significantly more customization options than the Seikret. [/spoiler] Your Palico can wear armor and wield weapons to match your own if you'd like. [spoiler] Your Seikret, on the other hand, has very limited armor options—even with the DLCs (I don’t own them, but they come with two armor sets for the Seikret). [/spoiler] These aren't the only companions you’ll meet and have by your side, but these three will always be with you on your adventures.

I feel that the price of the game is quite high, but for those willing to pay it, I’d say it’s mostly worth it. Do I wish it were cheaper? (I wish everything was cheaper) Yes. Do I think the price makes sense? For the most part. Do I think the price with the DLCs is worth it? Absolutely not.

[b]Overall rating :[/b] 7.9/10

name: Monster Hunter Wilds
review:
At the beginning, I felt like the game was okay, but the more I play and the more updates come out, the more annoyed I feel about it.
The biggest thing specifically, which annoys me the most probably, is that the Monster Hunter Team just keeps ignoring player feedback.
If you haven’t played any Monster Hunter game before, ignore this review and just play World. If you have, and you’re curious about Wilds, well, here is the list of things that I don’t like:
[list]
[*][b]Multiplayer / SOS system:[/b] This could be okay, but the implementation is pretty horrible. If I were to do it, I would just give a list of SOS flared quests to the players in a table format, paginated. Filters above, most importantly, monsters in a dropdown list as checkboxes so you can filter for multiple monsters. Also, I would add one random join button, if someone just wants to play but does not care about what to hunt. The point is, the fact that I can only filter for one monster, and tempered/non-tempered is separated, is stupid.
[*][b]Way of farming:[/b] So, before this was not really an issue (though for some people it was), after the latest update (TU2), they have changed the drop rates for the newest monsters. Hence, the best way to farm the gems is to wait for an investigation that has the gem as a reward. To do this, you have to rest at the camp until you get one, basically playing a slot machine. This is stupid as hell.
[*][b]Artian system:[/b] Weapons as slot machines. I think every old Monster Hunter player liked the games because if you wanted an armor or weapon, you just farmed the monster until you got it. The artian system is just stupid. They made a better version of this in World with Safi, but in this game, it is just too simple and bad.
[*][b]Lack of Friction:[/b]
-Part I: I already hated the Palamute in Rise. This game just makes it worse with automove. The mounts just make it so you won’t care about the maps or anything else. Run to the monster, slay it, get reward, repeat. Basically making the game into an arcade-style game instead of an actual good game with atmosphere. Instead of an actual hunting game.
-Part II: Drop rates for monsters before TU2 are just too much. You can hunt a monster once and craft everything.
-Part III: Due to the lack of content, you can just blaze through the entire game.
• Difficulty system: So now we have strength levels. Why not just do it as before, give us the monster. Every monster should have its own difficulty. No need to overcomplicate it.
[*][b]Lack of content:[/b] I mentioned this above in my friction section, but basically every Monster Hunter game before had a ton of side quests, hunts, gathering quests, etc. Not this game.
[*][b]No BIG village/camp/city whatever:[/b] In every Monster Hunter game, you had a big hub area with great atmosphere and music. Not this one. I miss it. In TU1 they added the grand hub, but that is basically just the Gathering Hub, a different concept.
[*][b]Performance:[/b] Is bad.
[*][b]Ignorance:[/b] And as I said before, my biggest issue is ignorance. I knew this would happen – that they wouldn’t care about what the player base wants. They had their plans long before releasing the game, and they just want to do everything according to the plan. They release their title updates and call it a day, but don’t care about fixing the issues, the UI. This is a long lasting problem to be honest, not his game is the only victim.
[*][b]Tantrum:[/b] Also, I want to add that the Monster Hunter Team now feels kind of like children who have a tantrum. So, they ignore a lot of things, but if they don’t ignore something (miraculously), then they just throw a tantrum and go overboard. Best example is before the drop rates were too much, now it feels impossible to get a gem. But not only do you need one gem, you will need three for one armor set, then if you need another, three more, and one for the weapon. I feel like this is how they were at the office: “They want worse drop rates? We’re going to give them worse drop rates.”

name: Monster Hunter Wilds
review:
TL;DR: Save your money, play World or even Rise at this point with how this game is being handled at the moment. Forget "can your pc run Crysis 3" its "can it run MH Wilds at all."

Started from World, went to GU, Rise, Iceborne, Sunbreak, then now this.

Getting the biggest/most common complaint out of the way in regards to performance.

It's awful, not being able to maintain 60fps on even after testing it on everything low and my pc is pretty mid in terms of parts. (i5-12400F, 4060 88GB and 16GB 3200 MHz ram) before the most recent patch is pretty terrible. Even after this update the performance still has not improved and continues to show Capcom's inability to fix issues. I've had 2 crashes throughout my time with this game but that shouldn't happen in this day and age. Call this company Crashcom because boy I'm seeing a lot of people dip from this game for these very fair reasons. They claim to have been fixing it, but as of recent people have not been able to launch the game or run it at all even after trying to do fixes that Capcom recommend. 

Gameplay: Too much story and pointless dragging on and way too much of a grab on the ecosystem as a whole. I've hated this since World and still do, it doesn't need a huge story to be fun. Some funny quirky moments with Alma and Gemma but not much else and as of this update one of the cringe fest cut scenes I have ever witnesses in a video game, the fashion show. 

Combat is fun as it usually is, however focus mode in my opinion is just a freebie when it comes to aiming your strongest moves. Being able to turn on a dime with Great Sword for example doesn't feel rewarding as it does in previous games where you're rewarded for positioning and knowing a monster. This applies to a lot of weapons but Great Sword is the best example, You can take this as elitism if you want, but in the grand scheme of things but I don't feel like I've achieved much, just mindlessly pressed buttons and let the game mechanics do everything for me with one single button hold.

The monster fights are great, especially the apex monsters we first see. They do feel like the supreme predator of that region and their gear is fun. However if you want HR and the best loot, good luck because you're going to be farming them for the rest of the game, since there is once again no point to fighting the lower ranked monsters unless you need specific parts, but end game materials? No. Even after they give exclusive tickets to those monsters for their respective tempered monster level, Artian Weapons are a thing. 

Speaking of, Artian Weapons are a terrible choice of end game equipment, it completely takes away the need to farm any other type of monster when you have create your class, stats and etc and they require RNG if you want the best stats, making my previous point of farming the apex monsters all the more unbearable. 

The game also struggles with balancing difficulty, as you have people say it is too easy, other say too hard especially with the 7-8 star differences which I agree with, there is a huge leap and some monsters have more health than FATALIS in Iceborne when doing it solo. Fatalis solo has 66k solo health and some of these monster have 70-80k+ health. They are not even elder dragons and none are in this game. 

The hub is nice, but got boring fast, there is little to do after you have done all achievements - crown farming is even more tedious but faster - and there is nothing in terms of customizing a room, there is your camp but eh, nothing special about it. You can't place endemic life or what not. 

Final thoughts: This game needed more time to be made, it has been rushed out and it shows especially with performance and QoL, it is inexcusable.

name: Monster Hunter Wilds
review:
As a big fan of the series, i'm sad to say i really cannot recommend Wilds.

Starting with the biggest problem, the performance. There's no getting around it, it's absolutely horrible and inexcusable that a full-priced+ game runs like this. Based on the performance itself, i already can't truly recommend it. This is not helped by the fact that on a visual level, the game really looks about as good as MH world from a players POV, if not worse in certain aspects. 

The story is in all honestly very mediocre, which is normal for MH. The problem is that the game disagrees and REALLY want you to appreciate it, slowing down the pacing to a screeching halt in-between every actual hunt. So many of the story missions start with a way too lengthy section where you slowly follow a NPC on your Seikret, where you can't even entertain the idea of going off-course without the game immediantly forcing you back to the designated path. Playing through the story with my friends was a terrible experience because of said reason + the fact everybody needed to go through their own seikret tour every quest before being able to join. They somehow managed to make World's already extremely flawed and bothersome story co-op experience worse. 

The world and environment of Wilds is a mixed bag. On one hand, it's quite neat how there's a lot of life and activity going on in each map, with all the monsters, small monsters and endemic life. This however is a likely culprit for a lot of the terrible perfomance for the game, a trade-off that's simply nowhere even close to worth the cost. This is coupled with the fact you barely can appreciate it because of the introduction of the seikret. 

I'm quite disappointed in the map design if i'm to be honest. Overall i think Wilds may have some of the worst maps in the series. Despite having played for more than a hundred hours i barely know how to actually navigate or remember much about each map, something that never was a problem in Rise or World, with the exception of the inner areas of the ancient forest in world. 

The cause i believe is the inclusion of the Seikret, a mount that automatically tracks and travels to the target no matter where it is. There's 2 major problems the Seikret introduce from a world design level. 

1. The designers thought that for some reason it was a good idea to fill each map with routes that can ONLY be traversed by seikret, making on-foot exploration almost completely unviable in a large amount of cases. 
2. The fact that seikret just automatically walks to the monster means you don't ever really need to learn the maps, or their layouts. I find this feature a very odd inclusion, as it makes all the work and effort done on each map essentially null and void, as their no reason to actually explore, learn and expeirence the environment. 

The core of the gameplay is still really good and solid, it is MH after all. It does however have some major issues. 
1. The roster, while one of the more varied in terms of species and types of monsters, is simply not big enough. 

2. Some of the weapon reworks have simply made the weapons less fun or unique. My personal go-to example is the bowguns, which feels absolutely gutted in terms of customization and variety. 

3. wounds are a interesting mechanic that has been implemented very badly imo. Wounds appear and trigger constantly on essentially any pre-not top of endgame monster, often times causing them to be essentially be stagger-locked to death without much thought from the player. 

Ironically the problem is the opposite for any of the newer endgame monsters, where wounds are so rare that they barely even exists, making them almost feel like a none-mechanic. It jumps from being a mechanic that completely cripples a monster, to barely even being a factor in the hunt at all. 

As a final note, i will say that i appreciate that the developers have been very open regarding getting feedback and adapting their future content to it. It doesn't however save the game from its issues, especially regarding the performance. Which has slightly improved, but also becomes worse, at the same time. For example, i got a friend that has experienced constant crashes since TU1, and can literally not even a hunt a lot of time without crashing since TU2.

name: Monster Hunter Wilds
review:
A great open world without any exploration, loads of content that goes by way too fast, some of the best hunts in the entire franchise with a combat system that removes everything that made monster hunter special in the first place.

The progression system, that all monster hunter games have been praised for, got mostly removed in favor of a generic, intrusive story that punishes you for exploring the world they created and instead puts you on a set of rails while constantly playing voice lines that remind you how fun it is to explore these new lands. If you want to go against the intended gameplay and run off to explore on your own you will be rewarded with horrible mount controls that have to be manually changed to be usable, barely any monsters you havent seen yet and active discouragement for hunting them early, large and empty maps that were clearly designed to be rushed through on autopilot and constant voiceline reminders to go back to the story.

Most monsters are extremely well designed both in terms of visuals and mechanics but since there is absolutely no friction or downtime in the hunts you never get more than 15 minutes to enjoy and think about each one before the story sweeps you off your feet to throw you directly in front of the next one. Each monster drops enough materials to craft everything you need to progress, making for an incredibly shallow experience.

Most of the new monsters have incredible movesets and the reused ones recieved great updates that make them more flashy and impressive overall. Sadly, this doesnt matter for most of them since you get enough hyper armor and defense to ignore most of their moveset until you reach late high rank. Instead of having a ton of incredibly diverse weapons which all have their up- and downsides everything got a counter, guardpoint or perfect dodge to trivialize most encounters.
perfect guards are the worst example of this. normally, the punishment for missing a counter or dodge is getting hit with the full force of an attack. when you mess up a perfect guard your punishment is blocking the attack normally instead.
Focus mode makes the game more accessible and makes trying out new weapons far less intimidating. Thats both a good and a bad thing. the ability to aim your attacks takes away a main feature of older games, that being positioning and planning. A TCS, for example, used to be very hard to hit but do a ton of damage compared to any other attack in the game but hitting them repeatedly is now easier than ever, meaning the damage had to be scaled down to compensate and taking away a lot of the satisfaction of the damage itself and of becoming good enough to consistently land them.
The wound system also doesnt help with this, giving you a shortcut to do a free TCS (or level up your weapons gauges) and prevent the monster from moving at all for a couple of seconds. 
Clutch claw was by no means a good mechanic but, fundamentally, it felt more earned than a wound. wounds just seem to appear after a while and you decide when the monster stops in its tracks, whereas a clagger felt similar to getting a trip or stun and rewarding you with the choice to capitalize on a monster being knocked back.

My last two points are less important to me but they still impact my enjoyment and so i will mention them.

The Effects in this game are downright horrible.
the only visual indication that you hit a monster is a bit of dust and a number. We went from massive blood splatters, screen filling critical flashes and explosions of scales and debris flying off a monster to extremely minimalistic, barely noticeable pool noodle whacks.
Other effects like fov changes, wind particles, screen shake, light flashes and hitstop have been removed or tuned down compared to older titles as well (especially noticeable in SAED)
The sound effects might be even worse. hitting a good hitzone sounds far less satisfying than in monster hunter games from 10 years ago on the 3ds. It seems to me that they kept the satisfying, juicy hit sounds for only wounds but hitting wounds is very rare and they break after a few hits anyways so its not a good replacement.

The performance. Everyone knows. This is the worst running game ive ever played when compared to the visuals im getting.

Overall i think this game has incredible potential for a master rank expansion and the monster roster is among the best base games in monster hunter history but if these isues arent resolved, either officially or through mods, i just cant see myself enjoying this game more than any of the older titles.

If youre new to this franchise, play world/iceborne and maybe rise/sunbreak until the Master rank expansion for this game comes out in about a year before playing this. The game will be much better optimized, have far more content and the community will have calmed down until then.

review:
Warframe is a game that rewards you for the amount of time that you invest into it. If you wish for a surface level horde shooter with fun abilities then it will give you that experience in spades, however, it also has the ability to allow you to delve deeper into its systems and lets you customize and maximize your arsenal until you become a walking army.

The story is serviceable in the beginning but in my opinion ages like wine as you progress through the star chart, slowly pulling you into an experience that I have yet to relive in any other Sci-Fi game I've played. While it does go off the rails at times it does so in a way that feels believable and maintains a sense of internal consistency that keeps you informed while still asking questions.

Each frame feels unique even though the devs have released over 50 differing characters, each with a unique kit that (while falling into a manageable amount of categories such as caster vs weapons-platform) still allows players to express their own uniqueness through their selection of frames and weapons. It is rare that any two players' loadouts will be identical to one another.

It is definitely a game I recommend everyone to play at least once and one I definitely recommend to anyone who loves long grinds, deep (though sometimes confusing) mechanical systems, and extreme horde shooters.
