name: Warframe
review:
I've been playing Warframe since Gauss update, which is around 2019 or so. Awesome fast paced looter shooter game.

I don't usually play third person shooter games with photo-realistic design like these, but this one is an exception. The Warframe designs which are like bio mechas are amazing, the gameplay is really fun, and it's not just about the guns, it also have melees and warframes abilities, which combines into unique builds. You can also change your warframes functionalities like strength, durations and range with mods and such. The cinematic stories are phenomenal and I still praise them till this day. The game also has a lot of game modes, which we will also come to this later. The game also has amazingly friendly comunity as well. This game is FREE TO PLAY while having AAA game level of designs, and you can grind premium currency ingame pretty easily.

HOWEVER the game is quite grindy, which is the least worst thing on the list.
You want to play with new stuffs NOW, but you have to wait 3 days for it to finish crafting, which kills off the hype.
Every content updates brings you new game modes, which is another content island that has barely anything to do with the rest of the game, with materials that once you have everything you can craft with that materials will, with no doubt, never want to have anything to do with that game mode ever again. Although a lot of content updates adds a lot of refreshing new game modes and well, contents, they all feel so different that it feels like another game entirely. Every time.
The game also lacks a form of "endgame content". By that I don't mean sitting in Survival for 2 hours killing level 9999 foot soldiers. By that I mean actual hard bosses. Assassinate missions are a joke, the bosses are forgettable, save for Eidolons, Orbs and Ropalolyst, which are not available for majority of the player unless they grind really hard to unlock them, not to mention actually be able to beat them. Railjacks are fun for the first hour or so, but it's also another content island which you don't want to have anything to do with. Asides from those, Liches and Sisters hunts are actually quite fun, challenging and memorable as a boss, and does give some nice uses or Raijacks as their dramatic final confrontation. The new Orowyrm in Duviri Paradox is also quite something too, but wayy too easy.
I stopped playing Warframe around The New War, but it's still fun enough to keep me coming back to the game occasionally because of the fun gameplay, the mechanics deep under it keeps pushing me away, and every updates with new game modes keep getting me dumbfounded of what is going on and what to do every time I return.

TLDR: very fun game with fun gameplay, but once you look deeper, you will see a mess behind the mechanics.

name: ELDEN RING
review:
More of the same that you know and love from previous titles like Dark Souls & Bloodborne. Awesome gameplay, beautiful scenes, and a very challenging experience. I especially love the many different weapons you can choose from.

Where Elden Ring differs most from it's predecessors is the open world, and it does it better than many other open-world games. Every corner has something new to discover. It could be a weapon, a skill, some lore, or even a path to a completely new part of the map. Maybe even a part of the map you're not really ready for just yet. But you can go there if you want. There is very little hand holding. And if you feel like you are not up for that part just yet, there is always some other place you can go to.

The story is like that too. There is no quest journal with lists to follow up on. You either figure out what you need to do, or you just go about your own way. It's tied into the open world experience nicely where sometimes you just happen to run into a familiar face in the middle of a field.

The downside to the open world is apparent though. Assets tend to be reused. There are a lot of bosses that you face many times, and many smaller dungeons that you've seen before. Several times I found some cave somewhere that I was hesitant to explore because I already knew what it was going to be like.

On the multiplayer side, I was happy to learn that you can play on online mode now without the hassle of being invaded! A very welcome change. The online features like the messages and 'ghosts' really add something to the overall experience. Unfortunately, invaders can still appear if you are co-operating with other people, and it's still an unbalanced mess. On the topic of co-operating, there still is no real coop mode. Which really is a missed opportunity. 

If you are looking for a great single player experience though, then Elden Ring delivers like no other.

An unforgettable achievement in open world map design. Extremely purposeful in it's layout, the lay of the land always feels intentional. Striking vistas are always presented as such, with clever gating often allowing the player multiple paths to arrive at these moments. The game struggles to keep it's momentum, and much of the optional content feels like a chore upon a second play through. Due to the nature of builds, much of your obtained items will not be usable or have very low impact on your character. This issue becomes more glaring when the prospect of replaying is so daunting. All in all one of the greatest modern RPG's for a first time playthrough, but falls off dramatically after it's secrets are plumbed.

Coop is extremely tedious in vanilla, and runs into the same issues of replayability as mentioned above, even when using mods like Seamless Coop.

review:
I’d purchased Early Access under the impression that this game would scratch a longstanding itch—which is to say that while there has been, in my mind, a trend of oversimplification across games of several genres, this one would offer depth and meaningful character-building.  Whereas other games gave (and continue to give) merely an illusion of choice, PoE2 would allow me to lose myself in all the different possibilities its system would offer.

For the duration of version 0.1, the game met those expectations.  The campaign was (and still is) 200% more time-consuming than it needs to be, but I found a very fun and comfortable endgame loop: run some maps, tinker with my build, maybe find a different mechanic or ability to explore, maybe change my build entirely (which likely entails re-gearing), rinse, repeat.  I brought four characters to level 90+, thoroughly fascinated by what each of their classes brought to the table in terms of distinctiveness—and intrigued further yet by what magic sometimes happened when, say, I took one class’s ostensible predispositions and superimposed them on some aspect(s) of a different class’s identity.  This constituted a freedom rarely seen anymore in character-building systems.

And then it was gone.  The 0.2 update saw an end to all of that by way of imposing arbitrary limits to the skill tree; the developers saw what they labeled as overpowered builds, and instead of fine-tuning the numbers/skills/options to rein in those builds—or, indeed, enabling [i]other[/i] possible builds to reach the same heights—they gutted the system.  (baby:bathwater::fun:unbalance)  Now, as with seemingly every other game, there’s merely an [i]illusion[/i] of choice; while the skill tree is large and visually full of possibilities, there are only a few and finite number of viable ways to play a given class.

That has been my primary gripe since the 0.2 update, but the game is imperfect in other ways.  (See: the numerous other negative reviews here; see also: the complaints on the GGG message boards.)

[b][i]“Bro, the game isn’t done yet.”[/i][/b]


^This is a frequently touted rejoinder to criticisms of the game, and while it’s very true that the game is still in Early Access, this trite remark does not take into account what has happened.

Imagine you’re watching a baker of some renown prepare a cake for you.  You’ve already paid for your share of the cake, and you—like the many others who have invested—intend to eat your own share.  This master baker creates the batter with some basic ingredients: flour, eggs, milk, sugar.  He throws in some cinnamon, vanilla, maybe something more unconventional, like miso. So far, so good.  Then he throws in some dogshit, shredded cardboard, and ground horseshit.

“The cardboard is an interesting choice,” a fellow customer says.  “But can we forego all the shit?”

The baker waves a hand dismissively.  He says, “The feces is part of the vision.”

“Bro,” another customer says.  “The cake isn’t done yet.  Let the man cook.”

Oh, he’s absolutely right: the cake isn’t done yet.  [i]But the baker has intentionally just thrown shit into the batter.[/i]


As far as I can tell, the “vision” GGG is pursuing is the much-maligned, never-much-played “Ruthless mode” of PoE1.  I wasn’t around for PoE1; I had to read about this failed experiment more recently.  Arguably, I played its most recent iteration.  I don’t like it.  I love a challenge, but that’s not what this game is.  On a fundamental level, this speaks to a core issue with the game’s current state: the developers appear to have conflated [i]challenging[/i] gameplay with [i]annoying[/i] gameplay.  After having wasted so much time on player trades that ultimately fell through, I see the lack of an auction house as the best example.  The game’s archaic trade system has players manually reach out to other players for gear the latter have made available for sale; far more often than is reasonably acceptable, trades fall flat.  From what I understand, the “vision” prescribes some measure of “trade tension”, the expectation being that a player feels a greater sense of relief(?)/elation(?)/accomplishment(?) when a trade successfully results in a gear upgrade—absolutely ludicrous.  See also: excessively large maps, experience loss on character death, extreme scarcity in useful loot, invisible one-shots, etc, etc, etc.  In keeping with this design philosophy, they could make players solve a prolonged series of CAPTCHAs before they’re allowed to log in: fire hydrant, crosswalk, bus, bus, motorcycle, fire hydrant, fire hydrant, traffic light, bus, bus, bus, bus, bus, bus, motorcycle…  Pass the images through a dark fantasy filter and boom, “challenging” gameplay!  

The bottom line is that GGG is making this game as slow and as cumbersome and as otherwise artificially “challenging” as its player base will allow.  If that’s your jam, then shit, more power to you.  Me, I can’t recommend this nonsense—even after all the time and money I’ve put into it.  [i]Especially[/i] after all the time and money I’ve put into it.

Reader, I uninstalled it.  I’ll likely check back every now and then, though to be clear, the bullshit present in the game is there [i]by design[/i].  Maybe we’ll see something closer to 0.1 after the dust settles, but I’m nearly certain we will not.

review:
Pros.
The game looks amazing. Skills are neat. Lots of path options.

Cons.
The camera is way to close. Enemies are so close by the time you can attack, you have to retreat.
The controls are a bit wonky. And the starting character dps is too low. Way too low. 

This game may be amazing later. But if I have to leap between every attack during every boss fight and half of the normal mobs, I feel that I had wasted my cash. 3rd boss fight consisted of running in circles with 10 mobs chasing. The head of the worm shooting single target constantly or massive aoe acid. While the tail would smash you if you get to close. The idea is great. But a bit of balance for gods sake. With a start this rough. It turned me away nearly instantly. 

A partial fix would be make fights more than dash attack. Ease the early levels into the game play, if the direction will indeed will be forced into dash attack for all ranged characters. Zoom out. The distance of the camera shoud be at least 2x the current distance.

Had high hopes. Will check back in a month or so. I put as a no for recommend, because there is no middle option. Add a neither, and you may have better statistics.

The game should currently be free to play and feedback used for addressing major issues.

name: Path of Exile 2
review:
[h1]⚔️ Path of Exile 2 – Review[/h1]

[b]Path of Exile 2[/b] isn’t just a sequel—it’s a full-scale overhaul, a declaration of war against every ARPG that ever thought it was hardcore. Grinding Gear Games didn't just tweak the original—they built a beast that’s darker, deeper, and more mechanically intense than ever. And if you're coming from Diablo, well... [i]welcome to the deep end.[/i]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Strengths[/h2]

[list]
[*][b]Combat feels weighty and brutal[/b] – One of the most immediate changes from PoE1 is how satisfying and responsive the combat feels. Hits land with impact, movement is smoother, and enemies react with visceral feedback. Every fight feels like a gritty brawl, not just a stat check.

[*][b]New skill system, new brain pain[/b] – The revamped support gem system integrates directly into skill gems, allowing for mind-bending customization. It's still PoE, so expect spreadsheets, planning tools, and existential doubt about your build—but it’s also more intuitive and rewarding for those who dive in.

[*][b]Dark, grim, gorgeous[/b] – Visually, PoE2 is a huge leap forward. The environments are oppressive in the best way, with rich lighting, grotesque creatures, and a sense of doom that never really leaves. You’re not a hero—you’re a survivor.

[*][b]Class redesigns = real variety[/b] – Each class has a distinct identity now, not just in stats but in gameplay feel. The Druid shapeshifts. The Warrior builds momentum. These aren't just new numbers—they’re new fantasies.

[*][b]Free. Still. Forever.[/b] – No box price, no pay-to-win. Cosmetics only. It's one of the most generous AAA-quality ARPGs you’ll ever play for zero dollars. And it respects your time more than you’d expect—if you know how to respect [i]its[/i] complexity.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Weaknesses[/h2]

[list]
[*][b]Still complex as hell[/b] – While some systems are streamlined, PoE2 is still a labyrinth. Build planning without third-party tools is borderline masochism, and new players can easily drown in mechanics.

[*][b]Online-only, always[/b] – Like its predecessor, you’ll need an internet connection to play—even solo. Disconnects, lag, or downtime mean no exile for you.

[*][b]Early game pacing[/b] – The first few acts are dense and slower-paced. If you’re used to ARPGs that shower you with loot and dopamine early, PoE2 makes you earn every power spike.

[*][b]Inventory Tetris: the Sequel[/b] – The loot system is rewarding, but managing it? Still clunky. Still messy. Still full of "wait, should I ID this or vendor it or chaos orb it or…?"
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Overall Impression[/h2]

[b]Path of Exile 2[/b] is not here to hold your hand. It’s here to test your patience, your planning, and your power fantasies. It's a game where failure is a teacher, builds are a religion, and your 100th hour is just when things start to make sense.

But for players who want depth, reward, and a game that challenges you every step of the way? This is ARPG heaven. Or hell. Or both. And it’s gorgeous.

[hr][/hr]

[h3]Score: [b]9.2 / 10[/b][/h3]

A complex, brutal, and beautifully crafted successor. [i]Path of Exile 2[/i] raises the bar for free-to-play ARPGs—and might just bury the competition in a pile of socketed gems and dead demons.

I'll say my dislike of this game is my own fault. I should have done more research. I did not play the first game, and saw a bunch of interesting videos on youtube for this one. The early game is pretty smooth, and I had fun for 10 or so hours. 
I did not realize that item grinds are impossible basically. To make progress, I needed to start to find better items for my character, which is almost impossible through drops. So, I figure, I'll just trade for them, since I was finding good items. They just weren't suited to my character. Guess again. Not only can I not trade in-game, I needed to use a separate website to line up the trades. This is an absolutely staggeringly bizarre decision by  the developers. To deliberately forgo an in-game tradehouse is mind blowing to me. 

Now, I get that everyone who played the first game knows all of this. But to your average diablo or wow player (from back in the day), this is a very jarring and unexpected deviation. And, to me, it breaks the game. I can see no future where I sink any more hours into something so  frustrating to interact with.

review:
I wish I could have given a good recommendation for the game, since I really enjoyed it, well, up to patch 0.2.
This new patch was supposed to bring many excellent changes and improvements to the game, but made it much worse:
1. The worst offender is that the game performance tanked, where it is no longer possible to play the game. On my i7-7700 and GTX 1080Ti I get barely non-stable 30 fps on the lowest settings, that includes both FSR on and off.
It seems that the major bottleneck is actually the network utilization, that varies drastically without any visible reason.

2. Instead of buffing lesser builds so there will be a variety of options, they nerfed many decent builds, making the game feel slower, which was already the case; Now it just slow as a slug. One of my friends is a tank-build, and he had [b]ONE[/b] good skill that had a really long cooldown. Now it is based on gaining stacks of "glory" which are almost impossible in our co-op play, making his game not that interesting (again, instead of [b][i]buffing[/i][/b] the melee builds that were under-powered before).

3. Random crashes (both crash to desktop and crash to login screen), sometimes multiple crashes in short succession.

They did insert some interesting new things, but in the current state it is impossible to enjoy these.
IMO they should have reverted to the pre 0.2 patch, and give it much more time in the oven, which is the standard in any other software-related field, but they just kept it as-is, and there is no major patch addressing all of these in the near future, since they are trying to refocus, which is more than okay, but [b]it is not okay to freeze your game in unplayable state[/b].

name: Path of Exile 2
review:
Path of Exile 2: Yeah, It’s Got Me.

I didn’t plan on getting pulled into this. Figured I’d give it a shot, maybe mess around for a couple hours and move on. But Path of Exile 2 got its hooks in fast.

First off, the combat’s way better. Like, noticeably. It actually feels like I’m doing something when I attack—not just melting mobs with screen spam. Hits land harder, timing matters, and for once, I can actually see what’s happening. It’s still chaos, but it’s cleaner chaos. The good kind.

The skill system? Still a damn spiderweb, but it makes more sense now. It feels like they finally figured out how to keep the depth without making it completely unreadable to anyone without a PhD in tooltip analysis. You still have to sit with it a bit, but once it clicks, you start seeing the layers. Dangerous layers.

Visually, the game looks great. Huge step up. Lighting, animations, even just how the world feels—it all adds weight to the experience. Some of the boss fights are straight-up intense. You’re not just burning through health bars, you’re reacting, adapting, probably dying, then trying again with an actual plan.

And yeah, the economy’s still a weird fever dream of orbs and bartering and "what even is money in this game?" but whatever. That’s part of it. PoE’s always been unapologetically dense, but this time it feels like it actually wants you to learn it instead of gatekeeping you out of spite.

I’ve mostly been playing solo, testing builds, dying a lot, and somehow enjoying it. There’s something addicting about getting wrecked and immediately thinking, “Okay but what if I…” and suddenly it’s 2 a.m.

Is it perfect? Nah. It still expects a lot from you. But when it clicks, it really clicks.

🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟 9.5/10 – A Dark, Deep, and Dazzling Evolution of the ARPG Genre

Path of Exile 2 takes everything that made the original a cult classic and cranks it up to a level that’s borderline legendary. Grinding Gear Games has delivered a brutal, beautiful, and brilliantly complex action RPG that is both a love letter to veterans and an invitation to new players.

First off — the visuals are stunning. The world is darker, moodier, and more atmospheric than ever. Every spell, attack, and environment drips with detail and artistic care. It feels like you're truly in a dying, cursed world fighting for scraps of hope.

The combat system has been completely reworked and it feels amazing. It's heavier, more deliberate, and incredibly satisfying. New weapon types, animation fluidity, and skill interactions make every fight feel impactful. Whether you’re smashing skulls with a two-hander or casting intricate spell combos, the responsiveness and depth are unmatched.

But where PoE 2 really shines — as always — is its character build freedom. The new passive skill tree system and gem revamp give you even more control and creativity over your build, without overwhelming new players. Want to make a frost-slinging archer who also summons minions? Do it. The combinations are endless, and every one feels viable in the right hands.

The storytelling has also taken a big leap forward. The campaign is more cinematic and engaging, with improved voice acting, better pacing, and some truly memorable bosses and moments.

And yes, it’s still free to play, with an ethical monetization model that respects your time and wallet — a rarity these days.

Whether you’re a returning exile or a newcomer, Path of Exile 2 is everything you hoped for and more. It's gritty, smart, insanely deep, and most importantly — fun. This is the ARPG we’ve all been waiting for.

its hard for me to justify giving this game higher marks because of it being in Early Access. However, i think this game is heading in the right direction with changes to loot drops, continual class balancing and end game adjustments. 
I think adjustments need to still be made. 
#1 the staff, spear, and quarter staff sizes. visually in the character hand they look the same  but q'staff is 8 inventory slots, 2 sockets, a staff is 4 vertical slots 2 sockets, spears are 4 vertical slots and 1 socket. IMO there should be uniformity between these. all 4 slots vertical or all 8 slots, all 1 socket or all 2 socket.
#2 This may be in the to be released 3rd sorc ascendancy but fire sorc ascendancy needs to be a thing. 
#3 more class balances. my ice leap slam titan warrior destroys everything. my fireball infernalist not so much. 
#4 random loot is fine and all but there needs to be a way to specialize an exact piece of loot. I.E. a spear with a physical numerical increase, a physical % increase, +levels to Melee + to crit damage and +to crit chance. Maybe that's god's gift to spears but there's no way to actually craft it. unless im missing something?
#5 Uniques are great to have but are outgrown somewhat fast. I am playing a crit bleed poison gemling that was using Pariah's Embrace chest piece. he outgrew it in 2 days. the stats are good on it but they fall off after a point. I wish there was a way to upgrade the uniques as the character grows. random idea but if something is 25 then it can upgrade at say 55 and 85 and it requires X amount of _____ Currency to upgrade. maybe this is forthcoming idk?
#6 Volatile plants. gold and river hag's balls. I played a map with 22 rare bosses, 15 had volatile plants. that 2/3. needs to be toned the F%&# down. gold drops of 17 are inordinate esp. in chaos temple. i see 17 or multiple of 17 (24,51,68 etc.) more than any other denomination. the river hags inst-death balls are crazy and will kill you in like 2 seconds. drowned city can be bad if you get stuck or surrounded and cant dodge roll out. the amount of time it takes the ball to kill you should be extended, imo.

name: Baldur's Gate 3
review:
I actually borrowed this game from a friend before securing a copy for myself, because I just couldn't wait until I had the funds to spare. When I tell you that I easily poured 200 hours into this grand love-letter to Dungeons & Dragons before it ever touched my Steam account, I'm being 100% truthful. 

The complete package this game provides cannot be overstated. There's a character creator that can be used by fellow tabletop addicts to create as many characters as you'd like; a strong, moving, elegant story, which branches into so many different paths that you can discover new paths just by choosing a new line of dialogue, or moving a rock aside in the overworld; the music, which never fails to raise the hair on my arms even while I'm just sitting on the title screen or idling in camp; the options for companionship and romance with your party members, who feel, in the best way possible, like real human beings, people who can strive towards heroic greatness or follow you down a dark path to villainous ruin; the countless non-playable characters that bring the world to life; the ability to start a playthrough from the perspective of ALL the major companions rather than making a character of your own; and, last but certainly not least, the addition of a SECOND main storyline via the Dark Urge origin option, which deviates from the default story just enough to give you a brand new experience. This game eclipses its market price several times over. It's simply astonishing.

Oh, and there's cross-platform multiplayer now, in case you've ever wanted to throw your friend's lovingly-crafted D&D character into a chasm.

Buy this game. Play it, love it, share it with your friends. Send love to the voice actors, the scenario writers, artists, and programmers - everyone at Larian, really. Baldur's Gate 3 is a one-of-a-kind masterpiece that everyone should try at least once.

"Shining star of mine, hold tight,
Don't fight the power."

The game is an utter memory and power hog though.

Occasionally, the graphics card just stops and the monitor goes black with no data input. 
I see that this is a known issue in the forums. I've been doing the recommended clearing the cache and lowering the screen resolution. Which Sucks, because that was one of the selling points of the game. 
But this would only stop the Black Screen for a little bit. 
Multiple times a week, I have to hard shut down and restart. Sometimes I even have to switch monitor ports and reinstall the drivers. 
And NO ONE has offered a fix. 
Now, this black screen thing has started outside of playing BG3, So I have had to stop playing it and remove it from my computer. 
Great job guys.

review:
This game used to be innovative, you actually had to think about what moves to throw out and specific times, now it's Chess with extra steps. New Characters are great and all but this game feels like 2D For Honor, new character comes out completely busted and it takes months for it to be fixed. There is an obvious favouritism when it comes to weapons, a lot of time and effort seems to go into developing weapons with the most free shit to give, i.e Scythe, Boots, Orb and Gauntlets. I understand changes are inevitable but at the same time, I feel like the devs are smoking some new kinda Crack that we don't know about. This game is built with the pros in mind, the pros playtest new shit and features and provide feedback that is advantageous to them and not the casual player. I started playing way back in the beta with the Founders and Friends Pack, I know most of the old OCE top pros and still talk to a few of them and we all share the same opinion, this game had a magic that was individual to it when it first released and in its first few years, the Ubisoft got involved and it was all downhill from there.

I wanted to write a positive review but in all honesty, the game is toxic as shit, Ranked is broken and I can't queue without getting someone at least 50-100 ELO higher then me, too many weapons are prioritised and a lot of others are left in the dust, allowing for players to abuse superior frame data and hitboxing with no notable change for some years now, it is clear that the dev team only care about new charactes, colours, merch, tournaments and battlepasses. I truly wanted to come back and give it another go, but the magic just isn't there anymore.

name: Brawlhalla
review:
1990s Flash game graphics meets platform fighter that takes the fun out of platform fighters.  

Characters aren't really that unique as it is all about weapons.  A "character" is a combination of weapons shared across a ton of the cast, and diff stats, and some "signature moves" which are abused by lower rank players and higher rank players use them rarely.   The characters lack personality or flair, and seem to just be references to something that already exists or skinned as a crossover and seems very lazy.

No blocking/shielding of any kind so gameplay turns into lots just pressing buttons, but don't worry, it's hard to punish it most the time so it's just how the game is played, in fact if you can bait people to try to punish you it's your advantage.

The game has nothing to reward fighting, so you just move around trying to bait each other into a something predictable.  Prediction and just trying stuff are the main aspects of this game, which make it flat and uninteresting compared to the pre-emptive, reactive and hitting waiting/unreactive 3 structure of traditional fighting games.

Jumps are super floaty.  Dodge is the ONE defensive mechanic of the game and there's constant RPS is built around "dodge or not".

Constant shoe ins to whatever crossover they can get.  So you can't even tell what character you're playing against by visuals half the time.  

Keeps some of the annoying aspects of platform fighters like edge guarding which if you're not a fan of that, then it also has weapon guarding just in case you didn't get enough guarding.  

Fun if you like to just chill and swing at people I guess.  For me though, playing it I feel my soul leaving my body looking for something else to do.  

I would have eliminated it from my list of games to ever play on the lazy art direction alone but got roped into trying it for almost 18 hours due to other people wanting me to try it.  I'm not sure how a game surviving off selling cosmetics has worked so long for them with a game this ugly.  I can't even tell if something is a leg, foot, or part of someones armor at times.  Where is their waist?  Do they have knees or ankles?  The world may never know.  The animations are jank too, and look done by SPINE or something else low budget.

review:
Lag and Connectivity Issues:
One of the most frustrating aspects of Brawlhalla is its persistent lag and connectivity problems. Many players encounter frequent delays, stuttering, and input lag during matches, making it extremely difficult to execute precise moves and strategies. The inconsistency of the game's netcode often leads to infuriating moments where one's inputs are either delayed or entirely ignored, leading to avoidable defeats.

Unbalanced Gameplay:
Brawlhalla's character roster is vast, offering numerous fighters with unique abilities and weapons. However, the game suffers from serious balance issues, with certain characters being significantly more powerful than others. This imbalance undermines the competitive aspect of the game, forcing players to gravitate towards a select few overpowered characters to have a fair chance of winning.

Toxic Player Base:
The Brawlhalla community has garnered a reputation for being toxic and unsportsmanlike. Many matches are plagued with salty players resorting to spamming, taunting, and disrespectful behavior, leading to an unpleasant and demoralizing experience for newcomers and casual players. The toxic environment discourages new players from joining and contributing to a healthy community.

Lackluster Development and Support:
Despite its popularity, Brawlhalla seems to suffer from a lack of consistent updates and meaningful content additions. The game's development team often focuses more on releasing cosmetic items and skins for purchase rather than addressing critical gameplay issues. This lack of focus on core gameplay improvements leads to stagnation and hampers the potential growth of the game.

Limited Game Modes and Maps:
Brawlhalla offers a limited variety of game modes, and the available maps are relatively small and repetitive. This lack of diversity can make the game feel monotonous after extended play sessions, leaving players craving for more engaging and innovative content.

Clunky Controls:
While Brawlhalla's control scheme aims to be accessible, it often results in clunky and unresponsive inputs, particularly during intense combat situations. This problem compounds with the lag issues, making it difficult for players to enjoy smooth and fluid gameplay.

review:
**Title: Destiny 2 PvP – A Competitive Mode with No Competitive Integrity**

Destiny 2 PvP has some of the best mechanics I’ve ever felt in a shooter. But despite that, I keep walking away from it angry, frustrated, or just asking why I even bothered. My main focus has always been **Comp**—and honestly, it’s a mess.

**1. Competitive Isn't Competitive**
Comp is supposed to be where skill matters, but it rarely feels that way. There’s no visible rank progression worth caring about, and the matchmaking is all over the place. You either get rolled by a full-stack or destroy a team that shouldn’t even be in your lobby. There’s no tension, no thrill—just unbalanced, sweat-heavy matches that feel like chores.

**2. Lobby Balancing is a Joke**
Destiny routinely throws solo players into uneven teams or puts drastically mismatched players together. You’ll go from being top frag in a close match to being bottom of the scoreboard in a complete blowout because the lobby made zero sense. There’s no real system trying to keep matches fair, especially in Comp, where it should matter most.

**3. Hand Cannons Still Dominate, and It’s Tired**
I’ve said it before: I’m sick of hand cannons. They’re always the fallback weapon, with insane lethality and forgiving TTK. It’s boring to fight against and feels like every loadout comes down to “what’s your favorite hand cannon?” I want variety, not forced meta worship.

**4. Matchmaking is All or Nothing**
It’s either:

* You stomp.
* You get stomped.
  Very few matches actually feel fair or engaging. The system doesn’t seem to care about maintaining a decent skill range—it just throws players together and hits start. Especially in solo Comp, it becomes a mental grind instead of fun competition.

**5. No Incentive to Play, No Respect for Your Time**
There’s no real reward for playing PvP. Nothing meaningful to chase. Even when I *do* have a good match, I don’t walk away feeling like I earned anything—or improved. There’s no satisfying progression or recognition. It’s just a loop that eats your time.

---

**Summary:**
Destiny 2 PvP—and especially Comp—is built on solid mechanics but completely fails to deliver a competitive experience. Lobby balancing is awful. Matchmaking is chaotic. Hand cannons dominate. And worst of all, there's no reason to keep playing. It’s hard to enjoy a mode that clearly isn’t being taken seriously by the people who built it.

This is a great game with the best community found in any game in the world. The people who play and are dedicated to it are truly outstanding. No game is 100% perfect—I've been playing games for over 50 years and understand that well. Destiny 2 is something I haven't seen in any other online game. Players genuinely care, have fun, and are willing to help each other out. 

The game is always changing, as all games are, but the heart of Destiny 2 lies in its players and the overarching message of fighting for the light to become your best self. I've witnessed this countless times in the game, and while there may be concerns about its future, I believe that if we give up, the game will certainly die. I know I will continue to play until the servers shut down.

This game has inspired so many. If you need a reminder of its impact, look at Lance Reddick's interview regarding the game. He didn't just voice the character Zavala; he played the game with us. His wife mentioned that he played whenever he had spare time, even just before he passed away. Think about that—he played knowing he was ill and never complained about the game. He simply enjoyed it and loved being part of the community. 

Eyes up, Guardians!

It pains me to say this… but you have now officially missed the boat. If you haven’t played the game: it’s too late to start. If you have played the game and haven’t played in a long time, it’s too late to return.

I have many fond memories with the destiny series. Even going all the way back to the beta in 2014 on my PlayStation 3. The series has been something of a social getaway for me when I first started 11 years ago. 
I remember spending long hours grinding strikes, playing crucible, roaming on Patrol with friends to find secrets. I remember the ARG for Sleeper Simulant! I remember the Red War and “laser tag”. I remember the era of “Oops! All Handcannons”. I have a lot, and I mean a LOT of memories and hours between PS/Steam/Battle.NET. But unfortunately the fun’s over. It’s like the MCU Endgame. If you weren’t along for the 10 year ride from any meaningful jump-in point before: it’s too late to jump into the MCU now. The “big moment” has passed and the subsequent content is…mid at best, but usually awful. 
It’s been a fun ride, Destiny. I don’t regret the time or money I spent. I’d do it all over again. But I can’t - in good faith - recommend it now.

Do I recommend this game? 

Destiny is all time narrative shooter that has spanned +10 years and held my attention for much of it.

The gunplay is industry leading, it feels so good the review could honestly end there. Add in a healthy playerbase and the fact that this is maybe the best looking PC game I’ve played and you have one heck of a video game. 

The game is good, but the studio has become questionable. As a PVP main I struggled to stay connected over the last few expansions due to the lack of content. The PvE story had more questions than answers and some expansions felt like blatant filler. The PvP dev team was removed, and the updates to crucible had stopped. 

Witchqueen was an all time high and soon after Lightfall was an all time low.

This is a great game. Proceed with caution.

review:
Overall, I find this to be a fun game to play allowing one to experience naval combat from the 1900s to around just after WWII in a semi arcade like manor. The ships themselves look wonderful and the battles are really enjoyable. There is a great collection of ships both historical and those that were one in the design phase to play with. There is also a wide set of match types for you to play in.

There are some engine quirks that get annoying but become less so once you do some historical digging. A prime example of this is shell dispersion. I've gotten frustrated at what seemed like a perfect shot getting reduced to 2 shells out of 12 landing on the enemy ship. I then looked things up historically at a crack gun crew in WWII with computer assisted targeting considered a 10% hit ratio to be amazing. 

Most of the problems with the game in matches in my personal opinion have to do with the players and not the game itself. Yes this is a game about amazing and cool ships. But that also means this is a game about naval combat. There are too many players that think they should be able to lone wolf it without being sunk quickly. Naval combat has almost always been about fighting as a FLEET to cover the weaknesses of each ship type. Another problem is I have had many matches lost because more of my team doesn't know what they are doing or won't play to the mission than the other team. 

If you want to play I would know what each ship type is for and that it WILL take time to get good at each class:

Carrier- scout ahead and pick apart any ship stupid enough to lone wolf it. Gets lots of hate from other players who want to pretend that air power in naval combat isn't a thing. Enemy finds your ship you are cooked
Battleship- this is the high burst damage and tank of the game. fun to play but many of its players in random don't want to do their jobs as damage sponges  
Cruiser- this is the jack of all trades ship. need someone who can fill in any role quickly this is your man. 
Destroyer- A very useful ship that is vital to wining the games by grabbing the objectives and spotting for everyone. requires some skill to play well. would get hate from the battleship players if Carriers and Subs didn't exist
Submarines- play similar to destroyers with more focus on sneak attacks. Gets lots of hate because a good sub player can alpha strike and then dive to escape detection even if that is historically what they did. 

If you can ignore some of the comments in the chat at times this is a great game. I would also say that most of the players are friendly too. But you should be aware that this game takes time to get good at.

name: World of Warships
review:
It is a long while since a game has got me hooked like World of Warships (WOW) has.   

Apart from premium ships, there are many ships to research for free - you start out with access to four tier 1 cruisers and they play very well at early levels. The daily login rewards, battle experience, campaigns, etc. build up quite quickly.   

Certain battles are quite challenging. Playing against bots in co-op battles is easiest, where you can achieve c.98% success in winning battles - by comparison, random battles against players are tougher, where you might achieve c.50% success. Brawls and ranked battles make it even more challenging to increase your skill level. 

There seems to be a general rush to get to higher level ships but don't overlook the lower tier ships. Each ship plays a bit differently, with its own strengths and weaknesses - part of the fun is learning to handle them   and use them well tactically. The WOW official YouTube channel is useful for seeing how to vary play styles for destroyers, cruisers, battleships, etc.

I am loving the customisation (albeit most are paid features), with special commanders with voice overs, permanent camouflages / ship makeovers, and seasonal themes - these all add a role play experience (one of my recent favourites was the Heroes of Might and Magic 3 theme, which brought in some nostalgia as someone who has played that series).

One feature that is a bit limiting as a Steam player is that you cannot access the wider WOW community through a  Wargames.Net account - it would be great if there was a route for Steam players to access more of the community-developed content.

name: ARK: Survival Evolved
review:
Piranha killed my dino-bot.

That was the thatch that broke the brontosaurus's back. Everything in The Islands "easy" starting area #1 has eaten my face off at least twice. Dilophosaurs won't even do you the courtesy of waiting until you're dead, to begin feasting on your entrails. You're generally blinded by their poison, so you can't see it. But that's not as reassuring as it sounds. I made friends with them. I learned how to use a pack of dilos as a meat and hide harvesting machine. Remorseless and efficient, if a bit messy.

But to kill and eat my beloved dino-bot, saddle and all? Oh HECK no!  I might not have a mission in-game, per se. But I am a cro-magnon man on a mission. There is no achievement for vengeance, friends. Only surly satisfaction. They'll all pay for what they did to Mr. Roboto.  

Soon, I had cleared the shallow lagoon in the starting area. I built a raft. Time to take this fight to the high seas!  I built a cooking pot, storage, a bed and several torches for light and warmth. I would be a mobile, one man seafood processing facility. Making kibble, and never tiring of the taste of justice. I learned to keep to the shallows. I became a ghost. 

But I got lost. I keep away from land now. Getting off my raft would mean instant death. It's getting dark. I have only enough fuel to keep one torch lit. I can't stop without being attacked. I'm running out of food.

On all sides, I can hear monsters I don't have names for screaming as they tear each other apart. 

I'm scared.

review:
I have no idea what I'm doing, but I get to ride dinosaurs.  Still mourning my first tamed dinosaur Berry, the Lystrosaurus who was mauled to death by a Rex.  RIP Berry.

----

The good thing about coming into a game late is the fact that there's a lot of fairly nice mods.  The bad thing about coming into a game late is that there's really no further development of the game, so what there is in the game is what you get, which is why mods are a great helping hand to improve your enjoyment of the game if you're not too happy with what the base game (and all its DLCs) has to offer.

Have played on almost all the maps starting with The Island - haven't fully explored the storyline DLC maps yet, but the free DLC maps were very fun.  Lost Island was nice - very big map with much to explore.  Ragnarok, Valguero, and Fjordur were the best of them IMO, and Crystal Isles was the worst (which is to say, I'll be revisiting it at some point to give it another chance).

Playing Ark solo has been a challenge, as I have seen it was built to definitely be a multiplayer experience just from gameplay alone.  Single player isn't impossible, as I'm sure with enough time and a robust enough herd (and a willingness to lose a few dinos in the effort), one can manage to conquer most anything.  Perseverance is key in any game that's challenging, such as when a Rex comes around to kill your beloved Lystrosaurus named Berry and then decides it wants to hang around your house and body for 2 in game days while you watch from a hiding spot across the river until it finally runs off chasing an unfortunate Parasaurolophus.

Get Ark: Survival Evolved and ride some dinos.

Stardew Valley isn’t just a game—it’s a cozy chapter of my life. I’ve farmed alongside strangers who became friends, and once with someone special who made every harvest sweeter. For a casual gamer like me, it’s a treasure. The gameplay is intuitive yet deep, offering endless things to do—from mining and crafting to befriending villagers. Oddly enough, I even enjoyed the fishing mini-game that frustrated so many others.

Someday, I’ll return to finally hit that 100% completion. Until then, Stardew Valley remains a warm, pixelated memory of teamwork, simple joys, and countless peaceful gaming days and nights.

name: The Forest
review:
I’ll admit it: I bought The Forest one night after a few too many beers. I played it for a bit and honestly thought, “What the heck is this? Trees, sticks, and weird cannibals?” The only thing I liked at the time was how it looked — and, oddly enough, chopping wood. There was something oddly satisfying about building your own little cabin in the middle of nowhere.

But everything else? It felt boring and just... weird. I expected more from an older game that so many people seemed to love. I thought it would blow me away — instead, it gently poked me with a stick and ran off.

Fast forward a bit: I gave it another shot... and, to my surprise, it wasn’t half bad.

Sure, it’s not mind-blowing. The story starts off strong, then vanishes like a neighbor who went out for cigarettes, only to reappear at the end carrying a suitcase full of emotional baggage. But as a survival game? It’s genuinely solid. Building shelters, crafting bone weapons, setting up traps — it’s all weirdly satisfying once you get into the rhythm. Just be careful not to spend too much time min-maxing every structure, or you’ll end up a spreadsheet hermit in the woods.

Yes, you fight cannibals — and yes, you might end up eating them. Survival karma at its finest.

In the end, The Forest tricked me in the best way possible. I went from thinking it was garbage to obsessing over finishing my luxury log mansion. It’s not a perfect 10/10, but it’s far from trash. I’d give it a solid 7 out of 10. If you’re in the mood for a bit of wilderness nostalgia and casual cannibal chaos, it’s absolutely worth diving in.

P.S. Play it with friends. It turns into a chaotic comedy show in the woods — highly recommended.

review:
Okay, so "The Forest." You crash-land on a seemingly deserted island, right? But spoiler alert: it's anything but deserted. Your kid is snatched, and suddenly you're in this terrifying fight for survival against cannibals and creepy mutants.

What's cool about it is how it blends chilling horror with classic survival. During the day, you're chopping trees, building shelters, scavenging for food – all that good survival stuff. But then night falls, and everything changes. The atmosphere gets super tense, and these terrifying, often smart, enemies start coming out. They're not just mindless monsters; they'll stalk you, try to outsmart you, and honestly, they're pretty unsettling to encounter.

You can play it alone, which is a genuinely scary experience, or with friends in co-op, which turns it into a wild, chaotic, and often hilarious fight for survival together. The story's there if you want to dig into the island's dark secrets, but you can also just focus on building an epic fortress and trying to stay alive.

It's not always the most polished game, and you might hit a few weird bugs, but if you're looking for a survival game that actually makes you feel vulnerable and throws some genuinely terrifying moments at you, "The Forest" delivers. It's a wild ride. Hope you have fun!!! :)

I see people say its "pay to win". It is PAY TO PROGRESS NOT PAY TO WIN !! Know the difference people! The robots look awesome and feel powerful, and the sound design is very meaty and thumpy, perfect for a game like this. Robots are extremely customize able with different parts, paints, and decals/stickers. Weapons need better balancing though. Using a phantom I can win a 1v1 with a titian with flamethrowers. Along with that is the fact that the difference between light/standard weapons and heavy weapons doesn't seem that big. We also need better game-play and more map variety. The current maps are excellent but gets a bit stale after a lot of matches. Custom matches and allowing the community to make their own maps with the current in-game assets and invite other people to play could be really fun, it would open up plenty of opportunities for the community to get together and make robot racing or parkour maps as well as flush out potential bugs that would otherwise go unnoticed. Along with that would be a custom match server list menu, many games just have an input code for custom matches and it really limits people and makes it a hassle for people to play them. Another opportunity for the game would to have a massive (10+ square km) ultra-destructible open world map that is primarily a cityscape that people can fight in (32-64 players max), explore, hang about and publicly show off their cool robots, maybe have some custom "chase the robot and kill it" missions for the battlepass or daily challenges (A server list menu for this game mode would also be advised).  It would just be really neat.

Overall in the game's current state I give it a 7/10 but that can easily be improved as the game gets more content.

A True Evolution of Mech Warfare

I've been playing War Robots Frontiers for a while now, and I can confidently say that this is the mech combat experience I’ve been waiting for. The battles are intense, the strategy is rewarding, and the customization options let you truly make your mech your own.

Monetisation - This game offers monetisation in the way games like Warframe do. But it it not in any shape or form Pay 2 Win. 

Tactical Gameplay – Every fight requires strategy, positioning, and teamwork. It's not just about firepower but how you use it.

Dynamic Battles – Combat feels weighty and impactful. Whether you're dashing between cover or unleashing heavy artillery, every moment is satisfying.

Customisation and Progression – The ability to modify and upgrade mechs keeps things fresh, allowing for different playstyles and strategies.

A Growing Game – The developers have been consistently improving mechanics, balancing combat, and adding content. There's a clear commitment to making the game even better.

If you're a fan of mech combat or tactical shooters, War Robots Frontiers is absolutely worth playing. With more players, the experience only gets better—so if you're on the fence, now’s a great time to jump in.

Would love to see more players join in and keep the battles going strong!

name: War Robots: Frontiers
review:
War Robots: Frontiers is one of the best games I've not only played, but ever seen. Frontiers doesn't only offer a satisfying and engaging combat system, but it allows you to make your mechs truly feel like your own creations. The robot building system is initially scary and complex, but once you construct your first build or two you'll get the hang of it and appreciate how limitless the possibilities are. The design of the game is simply fabulous. The graphics are gorgeous (and very well-optimized) and the SFX is superb. Every map in the game is unique in feel and strategy while also being packed with incredible detail, and there are even weather variants for the maps making each battle feel new. Weather/time of day isn't the only variable in the maps since the environment and buildings are destructible, causing the points of interest on the map to reflect the carnage that has taken place nearby. The balancing of equipment is good overall, although stats change between updates. However, I find that the changing of stats combined with the occasional introduction of new parts to tinker with allows for the gameplay never to get stale since the optimal setups are constantly changing. The developer transparency for Frontiers is exceptional as of now, although that may change after the actual release since the community will be much larger. The CMs (Community Managers) often engage with the community on Discord and Reddit, and it's refreshing to have that level of engagement. Whenever Frontiers is released – for free I might add – I highly recommend giving it a try, you will not regret it. 

Masterpiece of a game, 10/10

name: Path of Exile
review:
This game tries very hard to keep you playing as long as possible because it lacks content and is too short. The main problems are:

- The storyline is too short and can be finished in 10 hours. You then have to do it again 2 more times on higher difficulty levels for more XP and better gear.

- You can't easily respec your skill tree if you made bad choices. You either need to spend days farming items that grant you respec points or you can start fresh with a new character. In fact, experienced players always warn new players that "Your first two characters will suck" so that should tell you something.

- Higher difficulties make you lose XP when you die. So basically if you're too weak to progress in an area of the game, the game's logic is to keep you weak. The only thing to do is to farm XP for hours by killing monsters in areas you've already visited and cleared without too much trouble.

- Farming for better gear is a chore. The drop chance is the same everywhere. If you want a specific item, such as a better armor for your mage, you can't farm it faster by going to an area where it's more likely to drop.

- There's no auction hall, trading with players is done through the public trade chat channel and private message. At best there's a third-party website that sort of helps organize trades between players but it's not exactly convenient to use (at least it's far from as convenient as a real auction hall would be). This is obviously intentional to keep the players playing and farming for gear instead of acquiring it easily from other players, yet the devs have the nerve to say that the lack of an auction hall it's a feature intented to promote player interaction!

- There's a new "league" every now and then. A league is like a separate server that lasts a limited time. When the time is up, your character gets moved to the main server. You must make a new character to join a new league. The thing is, some unique items can only be acquired in specific leagues. So to get them, you're forced to start a new character with every league. Again, just another ridiculous way the game tries to make you grind.

- The game is incredibly hard (again, to keep you grinding and playing). In other games there's a point where getting more health or resistances than you already have just makes things easier but isn't required, but in Path of Exile you need to grab all the health you can in the skill tree and max out your resistances (all of them at the same time, because enemy encounters are unpredictable and monsters aggro you off screen).

I keep dying in areas of my level. I have a good balance of health, mana and damage but it's not enough to survive long enough to earn XP and level up. I could have maxed out my health first, but then I'd either be running out of mana after casting just 3 spells or my damage would be so low it would take me minutes to kill basic mobs. To reasonably progress in the areas of my character's level, I actually need at least a dozen more levels. It's just ridiculous, but again the game tries to make you grind for XP, gear and everything else or otherwise you'd be done with it in 10 hours.

I don't know why people like this game. I assume they got tricked into spending money and don't want to face the fact it was a mistake (the game is enjoyable in the beginning, the frustration only becomes obvious halfway through the second playthrough). Or maybe these players just can't afford to buy games so they're stuck with PoE and have to make the best of it. Or maybe they have so much free time that spending 10 hours grinding for a few levels isn't a big deal to them.

Either way, the objective truth is that this game has an awful design. It's nothing more than a grindfest. Honestly I tried. I really tried to enjoy the game and getting through the tedious parts. I tried to believe the positive reviews saying it was a good game, or that end game was fun, or that you could overcome the difficulty once you knew the game better. But it just keeps getting more grindy and tedious, and the difficulty is artificial and there's not much to learn that makes it easier. It gets worse and worse as you play. I got far enough to realize that the game has only 10 hours of content and the only way the devs found to keep people playing is to make them grind for hours on end for a small bonus. If that's the impression I'm left with after more than 80 hours of playing, I'm not going to stick around for another 80 hours just to see if it does actually get better at some point. I'm not going to spend dozens more hours testing yet another "good build" recommended by an experienced player (I've spent at least 20 hours researching information to get better and I'm still stuck). 80 hours of playtime and all I see is a grindfest. That's probably because [i]it is[/i] a grindfest.

So honestly, stay away from this game. It's not fun or enjoyable after the first playthrough.

Edit: Also, the community is just awful. There are a few helpful mature players here and there but for the most part it's just rude and childish people. I've never had to remove so many insults and one-line troll posts from a review before in such a short amount of time. I'll start leaving non-constructive comments up though, that way mature people looking for actual information about the game can see the problem for themselves. And I'm not even going to mention the stuff I saw in the game chat.

name: Path of Exile
review:
Path of Exile is an incredible game written by New Zealand developer Grinding Gear Games. The game puts you into the role of one of seven possible characters, each with their own story, that has been exiled from their homeland and is forced to try and survive in the harsh and unforgiving terrain of Wraeclast.

Graphics: 7/10

Graphically, the game isn't absolutely spectacular. In fact, it's dark, gritty and quite gruesome. It sets the mood extremely well and really gives the image of a dark, foreboding land where the people are oppressed and monsters and bandits are rampant.  Some of the areas in the game can be quite disturbing and really set the mood of the game itself.  Although, as stated, it is far from graphically superior, the graphics and the design work really mesh well with this game and set the tone the whole way through.

Music: 9/10

The score of this game is incredible. It really works alongside the dark, foreboding land of Wraeclast and meshes extremely well with the environments that the player is tracking through to give the game an atmosphere that is really quite gloomy, yet aesthetically pleasing.

Story: 9/10

The only reason that this wasn't marked a Tye Dillinger is due to the fact that you kind of have to really find the story elements by talking to NPCs, finding stories and graffiti engraved on rocks and walls throughout your travels and really listen to the interactions that are taking place on the screen in front of you.  If you do take the time to learn the story, you'll find an extremely engaging and in depth masterpiece, with an extrordinary amount of fluff for those of you who want to learn the history of Wraeclast and what has happened prior to the land being in its current state.

Gameplay: 9/10

The gameplay is absolutely fantastic. With a passive tree reminicent of Final Fantasy X's sphere grid, hundreds of skill gems, hundreds of different monsters and enemies and insane amounts of differing equipment, the cusomisability of this game is second to none that I have ever found. Although there are only seven character/classes to choose from to begin with, that by no means locks you into a certain style of play.

On top of all of that, new content is released consistently from GGG.  Approximately every three months, a new league is created, trialling a new mechanic and potentially adding complete new areas, enemies and bosses to the game.  That league will then usually be incorporated into the game in some way or another, eventually joining mechanics from previous leagues and making this game truly challenging.

GGG are currently also hard at work on POE, creating their biggest content update so far.  The game will be expanded to ten acts, up from the previous five. Apparently, there will also be only one difficulty throughout the entire game, making it far less grindy to get to the end game.

The only reason I have deducted points from the gameplay is that it can be extremely daunting for newer players and the learning curve is quite steep. This is offset by the community however, which I will go into more detail next.

Community: 10/10

The POE community is one of the best I have ever seen. People are always happy to help out if players are having trouble. Trolls seem to be few and far between.  The POE community is home to some of the best and nicest streamers I have ever had the opportunity to talk to including Ziggy D, LiftingNerdBro, Zizaran and Pohx.  These guys are always happy to help if they can and will generally take the time to help new players. They each have several build guides that are perfect for players that are just starting out and will help you get a hang of the mechanics for the game and eventually learn to stand on your own.

Cost 10/10

F2P!!! There is nothing else that needs to be said here. The game in no way, shape or form is pay to win. The only slight advantage you can get from spending money is to buy extra stash tabs for all of your loots, which are quite cheap anyway at about $2 or so each.  This game is easilly worth any money that you will spend on the stash tabs. Other things you can buy to support the game are mainly cosmetic changes to skills and items, basically making your character look cooler.  That's it.

Overall: 9/10

An absolutely solid game, well worth a shot for anyone who is a fan of ARPGs along the lines of Diablo, Titan Quest or Grim Dawn.

I hope to see you in Wraeclast Exiles!

name: Path of Exile
review:
Path of Exile is a decent enough online-only action RPG that sticks pretty close to the classic Diablo formula. It is also a great example of a free to play game done right.

The game is clearly made for the hardcore fans of the genre. There's a fair bit of complexity and very little handholding. At times the game feels downright hostile to new players as there are plenty of ways to permanently mess up your character build and the game does a rather terrible job of explaining many of the game mechanics. In practice you are pretty much forced to read wikis and guides unless you enjoy going through a lot of tedious trial and error.

On the other hand it's quite refreshing to see a complex character development system in this day and age when most games go for the dumbed down approach instead. The massive skill tree is certainly the most notorious example of this. I wasn't actually a massive fan of the tree, however. The tree just feels like a lot of added complexity for little additional depth. The skill gem system on the other hand is a great addition and offers some interesting choices between the different active skills and the various support gems. I would have actually preferred to see even more options and complexity here.

Unfortunately the actual moment to moment gameplay is rather lackluster and simple. While the character builds are complex enough, the actual combat is not very involved and you generally have only a few active abilities available to you at a time. This is something where both Grim Dawn and Diablo II do a much better job.

The loot system is pretty standard for the genre and not particularly exciting. The monsters drop a lot of loot but the vast majority is useless junk. Even most of the unique items feel rather underwhelming. I also strongly disliked how clearly the loot system is designed around trading items, something I personally have zero interest in games like these. The potion system on the other hand is a great innovation and one of my favorite features of the game.

Visually the game is not much to look at and the maps and monsters often look boring and dull. A bit more inspired visual design would have certainly helped. The game also suffers from rather serious performance issues and terrible optimization. Sound effects and music are passable, but not particularly memorable.

On a more positive note the free to play model is extremely well done. Most of the things you can buy are just cosmetics with no in-game bonuses. The extra stash space is really the only thing you need to spend money on, but the standard four tabs should be sufficient for quite a while unless you are a pack rat.

Overall I had somewhat mixed feelings about Path of Exile. On one hand it offers decent character customization and lots of content. On the other hand the actual gameplay is rather lackluster and the production values leave a lot to be desired. Still, it's almost completely free to play and as such easy to recommend. Just be prepared for a massive time commitment and a large amount of repetition if you want to reach the end game.

For this review I played once through the normal difficulty mode. Personally I didn't enjoy the game enough to push through the other difficulty modes to reach the end game. I also played a fair bit around the original launch, but I wasn't overly impressed by the game back then either. I'll probably come back for another look when the 3.0 patch is released.

The good:
- Superb free to play model
- Lots of content
- Good variety of different character builds
- Skill gem system is great
- Innovative potion system

The bad:
- Boring loot
- Good items are very hard to get without trading
- Bland visuals
- Poorly optimized
- Weak writing and utterly forgettable story
- Obtuse game mechanics
- Grindy and repetitive (which is normal for the genre, still doesn't make it enjoyable)

name: Path of Exile
review:
[h1]I don't have a lot of Hours on this, as I just started playing it through steam. I have been playing Path of Exile since June of 2012 http://i.imgur.com/jeP6URF.png and have thousands of hours on it.[/h1]

It is among the most amazingly awesome games I have ever played. Coming from Diablo 2: LoD, and the various mods (Valhalla, Eastern Sun, Median, etc) this game is perfect for me. 

* I will start here, with the things that I enjoy about it.

1. Diversity among builds. Want to shoot a thousand exploding arrows per second (Quill Rain + Chain/Greater Multiple Projectiles/Exploding Arrow/Fire Penetration)? Want to blast rays of fire that launch exploding balls of magma (Scorching Ray/Cast While Channeling/ Fire Penetration/ Multiple Projectiles/Magma Orb)? Want to call forth the fury of the heavens with a mighty scepter, smashing your foes into submission (Mjolnir+ Lightning Strike/Arc/StormCall/Spark/Multistrike)? The sheer amount of ways you can go about destroying mobs is limited only to your imagination. 

2. Story is great, very interestnig, and keeps you entertaining while playing through the game. Unlike other ARPGS of similar play style, Path of Exile is able to effectively deliver a quality story along with the extremely well done gameplay.

3. Scenery is dark and grim, gloomy, morbid, and full of gore. From corpse ridden beaches, ancient temples filled with undead and skeletons, destitute crumbling cities, palace cellars flooded with blood - ridden with heaps of corpses and twisted miscreations, echocing crystal caverns of golems and mutated freaks. The variety in enemies and terrain is very broad. 

4. Item creation, map alteration and creation, uber dungeons. There is plenty of challenge to be had in this game, thus keeping you striving to achieve ever greater power and push yourself ot the absolute limits of your capabilities.

5. Infinite replayablity. I have made probably 50+ characters so far, and each one gets progressively more powerful as I understand more about the game, the mechanics, and how to build them effectively. 

6. Temp Leagues + Ladder. Nuff said.

7. Constant expansion and content updates. The game is constantly being updated, minor balance tweaks, additional items, skills, monsters, maps, etc. It's amazing.

8. Grinding Gear Games are among the most amazing gaming company. Really really good people and they constantly interact and have dialogue with the playerbase. "How do you guys feel about X? Does Y feel right to you? If you could change X, what would you do and why?" etc.

[b]I could go on for another thousand lines but I feel as though I got the point across. The game is amazingly fun and addicting.[/b]

[h1]Now, for the things that, I don't necessarily "dislike" - but things that I feel may dissuade other people from playing the game.[/h1]

1. Learning Curve is incredibly steep. Your first 3-5 characters will be absolute trash. You need to do a bit of research on what to do and how to build effectively, otherwise you're probably going to get wrecked hard once you get to a4 merciless. Here is a beginners guide - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lEZtq6FSebE&list=PLjlRwdIo6SixoG_Bo5bhKCzZtOMVuVnJZ&index=8&t=8s

2. Repetition of acts, 3 difficulties (however, this will be gone come July - TEN ACTS ONE PLAYTHROUGH HYPE!) Going from Normal, to Cruel, and then to Merciless can really put people off. Myself, I'm used to it and have done it since d2 so it's just a normal thing for the arpg genre. GGG are going to change that though.

3. Item crafting is [b]extremely[/b] expensive. Like, unfathomably expensive. I have never crafted an item before other than throwing an alch and a couple chaos into a rare item. 

4. Currency is nightmarishly rare. I've found maybe 4 exalted orbs in my entire time playing this game. Two of them were just within the last week as well. I have only ever owned two 6-link items. Wings of Entropy, and some random rare 2h sword that is garbage. 

5. poe.trade is the only real way to trade. $Chat is a scam 100% of the time. Once they implement a real trading system other than posting shops online and checking the forums every 3 minutes, or browsing poe.trade for an hour at a time trying to find an item to fill a hole in your build this game will be just shy of perfection.

Those are really the only negative things I can think of that might dissuade a player from sticking around... the game is magnificent.

I highly, highly suggest you play.

[h1]Overall Rating[h1]
[b]10/10 - one of my favorite games of all time.[/b]

name: PAYDAY 2
review: Payday 2 is an absolute blast to play—a chaotic, fast-paced 4-player co-op shooter where the goal is simple: get rich or die trying. You and your crew pull off all kinds of high-stakes heists, from robbing banks, jewelry stores, and casinos to infiltrating art galleries, nightclubs, and even top-secret military facilities. You’ll be stealing everything from cash and gold to drugs, priceless art... and yes, even nuclear warheads (not joking). You can try to go stealthy or go in guns blazing (though let’s be honest, we all know which one is more fun). The soundtrack is pure adrenaline. There’s a ton of customization too, with a huge variety of weapons, attachments, skins, and unique masks to collect as you progress. The gunplay is tight, the gameplay loop is addictive, and there’s always another score to plan. One downside: a lot of the content is locked behind DLC. If you want the full experience with all the best heists, you’ll likely want to grab the Legacy Collection, which bundles most of it together. All in all, Payday 2 is a fun, chaotic ride that I highly recommend to fans of FPS games and co-op mayhem. So gear up, don’t act dumb, and enjoy the music.

💰 "Get In. Grab the Loot. Get Out—If You Can!"
🌟 Rating: 8,8/10

PAYDAY 2 isn’t just a shooter—it’s the ultimate heist simulator, packed with adrenaline, chaos, and endless tactical choices. Whether you're going loud or stealthy, solo or with friends, every mission feels like a Hollywood crime blockbuster gone off the rails (in the best way possible).

🔫 Gameplay:
Robbing banks, stealing art, cooking meth, or hacking servers—every job offers a unique experience. The gameplay is deep and addictive, with skill trees, customizable loadouts, weapon mods, and perks to suit any role. Want to be a silent infiltrator? A walking tank? A tech wizard? The choice is yours.

🎭 Freedom & Teamwork:
No two heists are ever the same. You can ghost your way through with suppressed pistols and hacking tools—or kick the door down and unleash mayhem with LMGs and explosives. But be warned: teamwork is essential. One wrong move and you’ll be swarmed by SWAT in seconds.

🎨 Style & Content:
With over 100 missions and years of updates and DLC, PAYDAY 2 is bursting with content. The visual style may not be ultra-realistic, but it nails that gritty, high-stakes underground crime vibe perfectly.

🎧 Soundtrack & Atmosphere:
The soundtrack absolutely slaps. Tracks like “Razormind” or “Break the Rules” pump through your speakers while alarms blare and bullets fly. Combine that with intense voice lines and ambient chaos, and you’re right in the heart of the action.

💡 Conclusion:
PAYDAY 2 is the go-to game for anyone who wants high-octane action, smart planning, and beautiful chaos. Whether you're running perfect stealth jobs or laughing through a botched escape, every moment is unforgettable.

🎭 Put on the mask. Make your mark. Become a legend of the criminal underworld.

review:
Absolutely Recommend getting this game if you wanna play a good GTA that doesn't have a multiplayer that is Rockstar's main focus while with GTA 4 the main focus is the story and holy shite is it the best story out of any GTA there is. If you played this back in the day as well on Xbox 360 or PS3 it is extremely nostalgic to be able to play all 3 games again. 

A problem I've found though and tried to look for with mods is the NPCs will get stuck on/in corners of cars, buildings, stairs, and doors, so you find yourself having to check on the NPC constantly and to get them to reset their pathing having to shove them in order to get them to get through or around certain things that they are constantly bumping into. It isn't just the story NPCs it is nearly all NPCs and if you are unfortunate to get Niko stuck somehow like I did you'll have to ALT+F$ in order to close the game because you are unable to cancel out the input for that action (unless car jacking). My experience of this is I shoved a NPC down and tried to buy a hotdog because was low on health and got to sit and wait for maybe 5-10 minutes maybe longer I did't count how long, of Niko running into the NPC on the ground that I shoved watching him bump into that NPC and not being able to pause, quit, or cancel that input for buying that hotdog, so I waited it out because hadnt auto-saved in a while and didn't wanna reset after buying all my guns. So pretty freaking annoying, but it buffed itself out.

I don't believe there is multiplayer in this, haven't really looked as been focusing on the story and getting all achievements for The Complete Edition, but if it was here that would be a bonus because this multiplayer was actually made to have fun instead of grinding (unless you went for the achievements back in the day, but all the current achievements you can get in the complete edition are story related, so no worries having to get friends to grind out the multiplayer achievements that's a bonus for achievements whores!)

Besides the NPC getting stuck and needing help I recommend GTA 4 for the amazing, gritty story it tells, the stories of the DLCs, and nostalga of playing on the Xbox or PS3. Absolutely pick this game up at full price or on sale and you'll have hours of enjoyment playing through this old gem that still holds up to this day and even more hours if you are working on 100% the base game and DLCs for achievements!

🌆 Grand Theft Auto IV: The Complete Edition – A Gritty Masterpiece Revisited

If you're a fan of open-world games with a strong story, memorable characters, and an atmospheric city setting, GTA IV: The Complete Edition is a must-play — even in 2025.

⭐ What makes it special?

Immersive Storytelling: Niko Bellic’s journey through Liberty City is one of Rockstar’s most mature and grounded narratives. It's dark, emotional, and unforgettable.

Realistic City Life: Liberty City feels alive. From the gritty streets to the dynamic weather and traffic systems, this version of NYC breathes authenticity.

Two Bonus Stories: With The Lost and Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony, you get two more full campaigns with their own characters, tone, and style – all tying into the main story.

Timeless Soundtrack & Radio: The radio stations are packed with bangers, hilarious talk shows, and a diverse selection of music.

🎮 Why play it now?
Despite its age, the game holds up beautifully with mods and patches available to improve visuals and performance. The storytelling, missions, and mood still compete with modern titles.

💬 Final Verdict:
A gritty and emotional classic that stands the test of time. Whether you're here for the action, the narrative, or the atmosphere, GTA IV: The Complete Edition delivers.

🟩 Rating: 9/10 – A must-own for any GTA fan.
